Applying a 70:30 split, lasso regression yielded the highest test R-squared (approximately 0.9131) and the lowest test RMSE (approximately 0.5008), with performance almost identical to LR and ridge regression. DT also showed improved test performance under the 70:30 split, whereas RF exhibited a substantial gap between training and testing performance. These results indicate that the evaluated linear regression model provides competitive baselines for this dataset. Further experimentation, including validation testing, will help determine the models' performance and predictability.

papers.title: Prussian blue and Prussian white thin-film electrodes: Single-step electrodeposition for anode and cathode applications
papers.abstract: This study examines how deposition potential influences the composition and nanoscale structure of Prussian Blue (PB)/Prussian White (PW)-family films, providing an experimental basis for assessing their proposed functions. Films were grown directly on Au/Cr/Si in a single potentiostatic step from a common aqueous bath at $-0.20$ to $+0.40$\,V versus a saturated calomel electrode, with a fixed deposition charge of 10\,mC. Electron microscopy, elemental analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy revealed potential-dependent chemistry and nonmonotonic morphology. EDS indicated greater K incorporation in lower-potential deposits, whose Fe~2p and Raman features were consistent with more reduced, PW-like environments. Surface K/Fe ratios varied nonmonotonically from 1.129 to 1.322 across the series, corresponding to 52.95--56.94\% K within the detected K+Fe population. Larger faceted crystallites at $+0.30$\,V contrasted with finer pyramids and cracks at $+0.40$\,V. Selected PB-like and PW-like regions had local cubic lattice parameters of $(10.31\pm0.10)$\,Å and $(10.36\pm0.10)$\,Å, respectively; their overlapping uncertainties prevent discrimination by lattice spacing alone. Cross-sectional maps showed broadly uniform framework-element distributions within locally continuous coatings. Together, these observations relate deposition conditions to contrasting chemical and morphological starting states without establishing bulk stoichiometry or phase purity. A literature-grounded outlook identifies ion storage, sensing, electrochromism, resistive switching, and ion handling as research opportunities requiring functional validation in these films.

papers.title: StreamSE: Neural Audio Codec-based Streaming Speech Enhancement for On-device Inference
papers.abstract: Recent generative speech enhancement (SE) models achieve high perceptual quality, but their non-causal processing and expensive computation make them difficult to use for streaming, on-device inference. We propose StreamSE, a 20M-parameter streaming SE model that operates in the latent space of a frozen pretrained neural audio codec. At each frame, StreamSE directly regresses a clean continuous latent from the noisy continuous latent while conditioning on its own predictions from previous frames. Enhancement therefore requires a single forward pass per frame and no iterative sampling or look-ahead. We further truncate the codec's residual vector quantizer (RVQ) to its coarse levels, halving the number of tokens per frame while improving robustness to reverberation. StreamSE is the only streaming generative model in our comparison, yet it matches or exceeds the perceptual quality of the offline generative baselines. Furthermore, the complete StreamSE pipeline runs in real time on a single smartphone CPU core. Our results show that continuous latent regression provides a practical route to generative SE under fully causal, on-device streaming constraints.

papers.title: Separation Theorems for Increasing Convex and Weak 3-Convex Orders on Real-Valued Random Variables
papers.abstract: We examine separation theorems for the increasing convex (stop-loss) order and weak 3-convex order. We improve prior proofs for the increasing convex order by using integrated survival functions. We extend the separation theorem for weak 3-convex order from non-negative random variables to general real-valued random variables with finite second moments via a constructive approach based on higher-order integrated survival functions. A counterexample verifies that the $3$-convex order and $2$-convex order chain does not hold for the weak $3$-convex order. Our results enrich stochastic order theories for actuarial science and risk management.

papers.title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: Deep learning shows promise for breast cancer diagnosis, but limited interpretability hinders clinical adoption. We benchmark ten ImageNet-pretrained models (ResNet50, VGG19, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, Xception, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet, ConvNeXt, ViT, and Swin Transformer) for benign-versus-malignant classification on the BreakHis histopathology dataset using a patient-level split, and explain their predictions with Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP. DenseNet121 performed best, with 99.4% test accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 0.999, and significantly outperformed all other models (p < 0.001). Transformer-based models trailed the CNNs. The explanations consistently highlighted nuclei-rich and glandular regions of diagnostic relevance. Combining transfer learning with explainable AI can thus yield accurate, interpretable tools for breast cancer diagnosis.

papers.title: On δ-derivations of \mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}
papers.abstract: We study $δ$-derivations of the finite-dimensional perfect Lie algebra $\mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}=\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})\ltimes\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$, where $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ is the natural $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$-module. For $n>1$ and $δ\ne1$, we prove that every nonzero $δ$-derivation occurs at $δ=\frac12$ and is a scalar multiple of the identity. For $n=1$, we explicitly describe the four-dimensional space of $(-2)$-derivations.

papers.title: Can One Hear the Absence of a Singularity?
papers.abstract: One of the central expectations of quantum gravity is the resolution of the curvature singularities predicted by General Relativity, potentially giving rise to effective black-hole geometries that are regular inside the horizon. We show that, for a very broad class of regular black holes including several known solutions, the quasinormal-mode spectrum in the large-overtone limit differs discontinuously from that of a Schwarzschild black hole, even when the regularization parameter is arbitrarily small. The real part of the quasinormal frequencies vanishes asymptotically, rather than approaching a nonzero constant, as generically occurs in General Relativity and other theories predicting black holes with curvature singularities. The asymptotic black-hole spectrum thus retains a distinctive imprint of singularity resolution. We establish these results analytically through a systematic formulation of the monodromy method and confirm them numerically. We interpret this phenomenon as a manifestation of black-hole spectral instability, whereby arbitrarily small deviations from vacuum General Relativity produce nonperturbative changes in the large-overtone spectrum.

papers.title: Superlinear cities, finite limits: Three characteristic scales of urban agglomeration
papers.abstract: Urban scaling research has established that many socioeconomic outputs increase superlinearly with city population, implying rising per-capita output. Although urban scaling models have incorporated infrastructural and dissipative costs, they have generally not identified the finite population scales implied by independently scaling benefits and diseconomies. We connect the classical urban-economic trade-off between agglomeration benefits and costs to a generalized scaling framework in which these quantities follow distinct power laws. When diseconomies scale more rapidly than benefits the model yields three ordered characteristic populations: the first (smallest) maximizes net benefit per capita; the second maximizes total net benefit; and the third (largest), at which aggregate benefits equal diseconomies. Their absolute values depend on the magnitudes of benefits and costs, but their relative separation depends only on the scaling exponents. We illustrate these relationships using published scaling estimates from several countries, and examine aggregate and extensive--intensive scaling across 102 Australian Significant Urban Areas. Aggregate employee income, rental payments and daily journey to work commuting distances for journeys scale superlinearly, although the aggregate rent--income exponent difference is statistically inconclusive. Mean rent per reporting renter household and estimated mean distance for daily commutes increase more rapidly with city population than mean employee income per earner. These findings reveal intensive differences obscured by aggregate scaling. The framework shows how superlinear agglomeration benefits can coexist with still faster-scaling diseconomies and produce finite characteristic urban scales without requiring benefits themselves to become sublinear.

papers.title: Residual dynamics determine dissipation in strongly coupled linear Langevin systems
papers.abstract: Interactions shape the properties of many physical and biological nonequilibrium systems, but whether collective operation raises or lowers entropy production remains difficult to predict. Here, we show that strong coupling suppresses irreversible circulation associated with the directly coupled degrees of freedom. In identical two-dimensional systems, this suppression is monotonic for nonzero coupling modes and guarantees a monotonic decrease of the entropy production rate (EPR), with the corresponding probability currents vanishing in the strong-coupling limit. In higher dimensions, suppressing the circulation associated with the coupled degrees of freedom does not generally eliminate all irreversible circulation, since the remaining degrees of freedom can still sustain nonequilibrium currents. The EPR of these residual dynamics sets the strong-coupling limit, providing a criterion for whether a given choice of coupled variables leads to lower dissipation than the uncoupled system. The approach to this limit depends on how the finite-coupling current correction aligns with the residual current. Further, we show that convergence to residual dynamics in the strong-coupling limit also applies to coupled non-identical systems. Finally, we demonstrate the predicted EPR reduction in nonlinear models of vertebrate hair-cell bundles and bacterial chemotaxis.

papers.title: pyTransRate: reference-free quality assessment of de novo transcriptome assemblies with current aligners and quantifiers
papers.abstract: Summary: The original software TransRate scores a de novo transcriptome assembly by mapping the reads it was built from back to it, with no reference required. Its last release (1.0.3) depends on Ruby 2.2 and on aligner and quantifier versions that can no longer be installed on most systems. pyTransRate is a Python reimplementation of the TransRate method built on snap-aligner 2.0.5 and salmon 2.7.0. In 5,031 paired comparisons (39 assembly-level metrics on each of 129 public assemblies), it reproduces the original sequence metrics and read counts exactly and ranks assemblies consistently with 1.0.3 (Spearman rho = 0.94 for assembly score, 0.98 for good-mapping rate), although its read-based scores are not numerically interchangeable with the original. It also reads gzip- and bgzip-compressed input directly. Availability and Implementation: pyTransRate is implemented in Python 3 and is freely available under the MIT license at https://github.com/macmanes-lab/pytransrate. It runs on Linux and macOS; snap-aligner and salmon are installed from Bioconda. Supplementary information: Supplementary data are available online. Supplementary Table S1 lists the assembly and read accessions for every assembly analyzed; Supplementary Table S2 gives per-assembly values from both implementations.

papers.title: Bridgeland stability and Gieseker stability I: Limit stability
papers.abstract: We study the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability conditions on smooth projective varieties. For each fixed ray in a suitable angular sector, we prove that an object of $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$ is Bridgeland (semi)stable in the corresponding hearts for all sufficiently large radii if and only if it is a pure $H$-Gieseker (semi)stable sheaf. In this sector, we identify the category of coherent sheaves as the limiting heart in the sense of eventual membership. We also identify a perverse coherent limiting heart in the opposite angular sector. The key ingredients are uniform HN-phase estimates for bounded families of pure sheaves, coefficient bounds for the coherent images of potential destabilizers, and a criterion forcing narrow exact sequences in the varying hearts to be bounded saturated coherent sequences.

papers.title: p-DCIM: A 28nm Probabilistic SRAM DCIM based Ising Machine for Near-Memory Context Selection in LLM-RAG Pipeline
papers.abstract: We present a fabricated SRAM DCIM Ising machine that performs set-level context selection for large language model (LLM) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). In RAG, the evidence-selection stage is increasingly delegated to repeated language-model reranking, which adds substantial energy to the inference pipeline. We reformulate evidence selection as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and solve it on a dual-mode digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) macro: the same multiply-and-accumulate datapath computes the embedding-similarity scores that populate the QUBO coefficients and evaluates the per-spin Hamiltonian differences that drive the anneal. The annealing temperature is set by a digital plane-count control along with the SRAM pseudo-read random bit flips, giving graded cooling entirely from on-chip digital configuration. The macro is taped-out in a 28 nm process [0.16 mm2, 0.41 mW] and is proposed to be integrated as part of the logic base-die in hybrid high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and high-bandwidth flash (HBF) stacks in a GPU package, where only the selected passage identifiers return to the host. Replacing the language-model selection pass with the near-memory Ising solver yields a macro normalized selection-energy estimate more than six orders of magnitude lower than the LLM-based baseline and reduces the evaluated total energy per query by 67%, while maintaining comparable token-level F1 on the evaluated examples.

papers.title: FLITS: an interactive, reproducible workbench for fast radio burst analysis
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are brief flashes of radio emission whose time, frequency, and polarization structure constrain their sources and propagation environments. FLITS (Fast-Look Interactive Transient Suite) is an open-source Python package with a browser interface for analysing detected bursts. It combines data inspection, interference mitigation, measurement, and modelling, including fits of the fitburst burst model, in a shared session, and reads SIGPROC filterbank, PSRFITS, and CHIME/FRB HDF5 data. The same routines measure larger samples from the command line and flag bursts whose automatic selections need checking. Trial dispersion measures can be scored by signal-to-noise, by burst structure, or with a smoothed-structure metric that also reports the range of dispersion measures consistent with the best one. Portable session files retain the selected data regions, excluded channels, calibration inputs, available results, input-data checksum, and software provenance, and supported measurements can be replayed from the command line and compared with their saved values. Uncertainty labels identify missing calibration information. A public reference workflow provides downloadable data and numerical checks.

papers.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_α$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_α^k$ on $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$ if and only if $-1<α\leq1$. We also show that, for every $α>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.

papers.title: GraftRay: Physically Based Mesh Insertion into Gaussian Splatting Scenes via Path Tracing
papers.abstract: Inserting virtual objects into scenes reconstructed via 2D or 3D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS/3DGS) is a key capability for content creation, AR, and synthetic data generation. However, realistic insertion requires the object to be seamlessly lit by the scene and, conversely, to cast physically plausible shadows onto it. Existing approaches either harmonize appearance in image space, sacrificing multi-view consistency, or approximate scene illumination with an environment map at the insertion point, which cannot represent near-field area lights such as windows and lamps that dominate indoor lighting. To address this, we present GraftRay, a unified method for physically consistent insertion of mesh objects into indoor scenes represented by either 2D or 3D Gaussians. We recover scene materials and surface normals with diffusion-based priors, and explicitly model spatially-extended emitters, solving their radiance in closed form. A hybrid renderer then jointly path-traces the scene Gaussians and inserted meshes, producing view-consistent shading, interreflections, and soft shadows. On FIPT, GraftRay sets a new state of the art, outperforming recent baselines such as ComGS and EAG-PT in rendering fidelity and shadow accuracy, while maintaining highly competitive rendering efficiency.

papers.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
papers.abstract: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. In particular, spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding are two pivotal tasks that underpin embodied AI and multimodal agents. However, synthesizing targeted, high-quality training data for these tasks remains difficult and costly. Our key insight is that these tasks share an underlying capability, which we call connecting evidence: identifying relevant visual facts, binding them to the correct entities, recovering their relations, and composing them into an answer. Crucially, targeted training data are far easier to synthesize for this capability than for these tasks themselves. To strengthen this capability, we propose EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-implement data synthesis framework that uses zoomed views of related regions within a single image to generate questions requiring comparison, aggregation, or chaining of visual evidence. To ensure quality, a reference answer is retained only when independent VLMs agree on it, and region-ablation tests discard questions whose answer survives the removal of selected regions. We then train base VLMs on the resulting data with RLVR, obtaining Zooming without Zooming v2 (ZwZ2). Although the synthesized data are not tailored to any downstream benchmark, ZwZ2 improves fine-grained and spatial perception, with further gains on embodied spatial reasoning, multimodal long-context understanding, multimodal agent tasks, and general visual reasoning. These results establish EvidenceConnect as an effective framework for supervising evidence connection and suggest that strengthening this shared capability leads to more generalizable multimodal perception.

papers.title: Another Brick in the Wall: Spectral Form Factor of Normal Modes in Horizonless Geometries
papers.abstract: We compute the normal mode spectrum and its spectral form factor for a probe scalar wave in smooth horizonless backgrounds. We first consider the BTZ black hole with a brickwall that hides the near-horizon region, which has recently been proposed as a toy model for a finite-temperature semiclassical black hole microstate. In this setup, the spectral form factor may or may not have a linear ramp, depending on the details of the brickwall construction. However, we argue that even in cases that do show a ramp, this ramp does not originate from level correlations associated with quantum chaos. Then we calculate the normal mode spectrum for a genuine microstate geometry (superstratum) and find evidence of chaos, both with a ramp and level repulsion. We conclude that the eigenvalue spectrum of normal modes can indeed serve as a tool for investigating the quantum dynamics of fuzzballs; however, the brickwall models are incapable of capturing this phenomenon.

papers.title: Constraining New Physics by Studying Single Top Quark Production
papers.abstract: This study introduces a beyond the Standard Model framework by adding a charged scalar particle, H_c, analogous to the charged Higgs in the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model (2HDM), but analyzed without the restrictive constraints typically applied in 2HDM scenarios. To assess the impact of H_c on single top quark production, two approaches are taken. First, variations in the production cross-section via the s- and t-channels are examined under different values of the model parameters, compared to the SM predictions. Second, spin correlations are analyzed, focusing on differences in the spin of the mediated particle between the new model and SM in the single top quark production via the s-channel. Within the framework of the simplified phenomenological model considered here, a significant fraction of the parameter space can be constrained by combining the two approaches.

papers.title: Quantum Annealing for Gamma-ray Source Detection and Localization with AGILE Data
papers.abstract: The detection and localization of gamma-ray sources via maximum-likelihood analysis is a complex parameter optimization problem. We address this challenge using quantum annealing, a computational approach that solves optimization tasks by encoding them into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian. Specifically, we apply this method to observations from AGILE's Gamma-Ray Imaging Detector (GRID) in the 30 MeV-50 GeV band. We reformulated the standard analysis as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. We tested this method on a set of AGILE observations generated with AGILEpy, solving the QUBO with simulated quantum annealing. The method reproduces the classical flux and position estimates within their statistical uncertainty and identifies the correct grid node among the candidate positions in 97% of the maps. These promising results demonstrate that quantum annealing could be used in this optimization problem, laying the ground for its deployment on actual quantum annealers.

papers.title: Guided-RLVR: Guided Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has shown strong empirical gains in improving the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs) on tasks such as mathematics and programming. However, recent studies have shown that RLVR rollouts often collapse onto a narrow set of reasoning trajectories, limiting the explored reasoning space. Motivated by findings that thinking tokens at critical steps serve as critical structural elements in LLM reasoning pathways, we propose Guided-RLVR, a novel approach that augments RLVR with a lightweight controller. The controller strategically injects semantically meaningful steering tokens into the sampling distribution, encouraging the model to approach problems from multiple reasoning perspectives and thereby expanding the exploration space. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks show that Guided-RLVR consistently outperforms existing RLVR methods while producing more diverse reasoning trajectories.

papers.title: On $π$-nilpotencies of finite skew braces
papers.abstract: Let $π$ be a set of primes. We extend the theory of left and right $π$-nilpotency in skew braces beyond the nilpotent type setting, and introduce the study of central $π$-nilpotency for finite skew braces. We investigate the relationships between these three notions, and a characterisation of central $π$-nilpotency in terms of chief factors is also established. This leads to the introduction of the $π$-Fitting ideal of a skew brace, for which we prove a local analogue of Fitting's theorem and provide a description in terms of centralisers of chief factors. Finally, we introduce the $π$-core of a skew brace and investigate its relationship with $π$-ideals and central $π$-nilpotency.

papers.title: State estimation for a hybrid rigid-continuum space manipulator system
papers.abstract: Spacecraft-mounted robotic manipulators can support long-term operability of orbiting assets by conducting tasks such as on-orbit assembly, repair, upgrade, and refueling. In this context, the integration of continuum/soft robotic mechanisms into space manipulator designs promises to reduce stowage volume and mass, as well as to improve operational safety through the inherent mechanical compliance of soft structures. This work presents a novel state reconstruction pipeline for a hybrid soft-rigid space manipulator, in which the distal link is a tendon-driven continuum robot. The estimation problem is formulated as a maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference problem over the hybrid manipulator's configuration, conditioned on discrete, noisy measurements from joint encoders and a vision-based sensing pipeline. The resulting soft-constrained optimization problem is transcribed as a factor graph, providing a compact representation for fusing heterogeneous measurements with the rigid-soft kinematic model. Furthermore, the adoption of the Geometric Variable Strain (GVS) approach yields a minimum-order parameterization of the configuration, a property expected to facilitate model-based feedback control design in future work. The proposed implementation is validated in simulation on a closed-loop trajectory where, for better realism, position measurements for the continuum link are obtained by means of a simulated visual pipeline leveraging synthetic photorealistic images. The state reconstruction accuracy and computational performance confirm the potential of the proposed framework for hybrid soft-rigid robotic applications in orbit.

papers.title: Discovery of a New Electron Spectrum Produced by Fast Cooling of Relativistic Electrons
papers.abstract: In energetic astrophysical sources like the gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and blazars, the relativistic electrons lose their energy efficiently through synchrotron radiation and inverse Compton (IC) scattering and can rapidly cool to energies below the minimum acceleration energy $γ_m$. It is widely known that such electrons develop a power-law spectrum $γ_e^{-2}$ below $γ_m$. However, this power-law spectrum is valid only if a steady-state population of electrons is assumed. In general, the cooled electrons below $γ_m$ evolve in a non-steady state and their spectrum deviates significantly from the power-law $γ_e^{-2}$. We present here a new electron spectrum $f_{\rm U}$ that describes this fast-cooled, generally-evolving, and non-steady-state population of electrons below $γ_m$. We consider two cooling cases: (1) when the electrons undergo radiative (i.e., synchrotron + IC) cooling, and (2) when the electrons experience both radiative and adiabatic cooling. We first derive $f_{\rm U}$ analytically and find an explicit expression of $f_{\rm U}$ for each cooling case. Secondly, we show that $f_{\rm U}$ is a solution to a Fokker-Planck equation in the entire energy range below $γ_m$ and derive a general version of $f_{\rm U}$ for each cooling case. We also compare $f_{\rm U}$ to a detailed numerical calculation of a blazar electron spectrum and find an excellent agreement for the whole energy range below $γ_m$. Thus, $f_{\rm U}$ gives us a general electron spectrum to describe the entire cooled electrons below $γ_m$. Our discovery of a new fast-cooling solution $f_{\rm U}$ below $γ_m$ may find it applicable in a wide range of energetic phenomena in high-energy astrophysics.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Discovery of CNOT Decompositions for Quantum Permutations on Constrained Topologies
papers.abstract: Efficient quantum circuit compilation is challenging for quantum computers, where limited qubit connectivity can introduce substantial overhead in the implementation of logical operations. Recent AI-assisted synthesis methods have shown considerable potential for reducing circuit complexity, but their role in uncovering principles that can guide the design of new deterministic compilation algorithms remains largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate this perspective for the synthesis of quantum permutations into CNOT circuits under constrained qubit connectivity. Using AlphaCNOT as an exploratory tool, we identify a recurring decomposition for remote transpositions that improves on the construction based on adjacent SWAP routing. For two qubits at graph distance $d>1$, the discovered pattern yields a topology-legal implementation using at most $6d-4$ CNOT gates, compared to the $6d-3$ gates required by the corresponding SWAP-based construction. We formalize this observation through a constructive proof to define Global Transpositions, a deterministic synthesis method that searches for a minimum-cost decomposition of an entire permutation into topology-aware logical transpositions. The resulting method subsumes optimal SWAP routing within its synthesis model and provides certified upper bounds on the topology-constrained CNOT cost. Our experiments also reveal circuits that cannot be expressed as concatenations of independently synthesized transpositions. Instead, these circuits exploit intermediate linear transformations that temporarily leave the permutation subgroup and combine partial effects of multiple logical operations, a mechanism we call intermediate CNOT fusion. Our results show that AI-assisted synthesis can support not only circuit optimization, but also the discovery of reusable identities, provable constructions, and hidden mechanisms in quantum circuit compilation.

papers.title: Learning to Code the World: Harness Evolution for Compositional 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing editable and compositional 3D scenes from a real image requires jointly reasoning about geometry, object structure, and spatial relationships. We introduce SceneEvolve, a framework that represents 3D scenes as executable code and improves reconstruction by evolving the harness around a small open-source agent. SceneEvolve combines SceneAct, a compositional semantic action interface built on parameterized primitives, hierarchical composition, and semantic spatial relations, with SceneHarness-RSI, which leverages a stronger teacher agent to iteratively evolve the harness using feedback from development-set reconstructions. Throughout harness evolution, the model parameters, action semantics, and execution backend remain fixed. The resulting harness provides a reusable reconstruction procedure that enables the small open-source model to reconstruct unseen scenes without parameter updates or teacher assistance. Across two in-domain datasets and one out-of-domain dataset, SceneEvolve with the comparatively compact Qwen3.8-27B model improves all four evaluated reconstruction metrics while reducing mean inference time by 47.0% relative to the base model. More notably, despite relying on a substantially smaller model, SceneEvolve achieves 32.3% higher reconstruction quality than the large proprietary GPT-5.6-Sol model, while reducing mean equivalent deployment cost by 59.8%. Furthermore, the harness evolved using Qwen3.8-27B also generalizes to Kimi-K3, achieving comparable reconstruction performance to GPT-6-Astra. The project page is https://haoyu-agent.github.io/SceneEvolve.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of tungsten armor and a liquid-lithium film as first walls for the HiPER laser-fusion chamber: thermal response, vapor shielding and helium transmission to the steel
papers.abstract: Tungsten armor and liquid-metal films, the usual sacrificial first walls of laser-fusion chambers, were modeled separately. Both go through one calculation for the three HiPER scenarios: NRL 154 MJ spectra scaled by yield, binned to keep each ion species' number and energy, a common deposition model, and a one-dimensional enthalpy solver with melting, evaporation and parameterized vapor shielding. In Demo (154 MJ, 6.5 m, 10 Hz), a 1 mm tungsten armor peaks 378 K below melting without neutron heating (275-319 K with it). A degraded near-surface conductivity can erase this margin, which also depends on the ion-spectra construction. The steel interface exceeds the 925 K limit, and the surface accumulates the 10^18-10^19 m^-2 helium fluences associated with the onset of surface modification within 10-98 shots (not a lifetime). A lithium film keeps the steel below 925 K from 44 um and below the 873 K compatibility limit from 56 um, more with partial renewal. Burn ions then implant helium; keeping the steel below 10^18 m^-2 for 10^6 shots needs 184 um, which binds in every scenario. The film evaporates 7.4x10^-4 kg m^-2 per shot (range 4.2-8.4x10^-4 kg m^-2, full renewal). Vapor shielding, with a nearly un-ionized vapor (Saha estimate), changes this by -21 % to +5 % for the Saha-supported stopping factor s = 1 and -34 % to +8 % across s = 1-2. Both walls are thermally viable in Prototype and marginal for tungsten in Demo. The deciding issues are tungsten damage evolution, lithium film survival and chamber clearing.

papers.title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
papers.abstract: Unsteady flow over a 30 $μ$m diameter cylinder at Mach 4 is investigated using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo across Reynolds numbers from 270 to 6750, spanning slip-flow to near-continuum regimes. Power Spectral Density analysis at discrete probe locations and Dynamic Mode Decomposition of flowfield snapshots independently characterize instabilities in both the stagnation and wake regions. In the stagnation region, a bow shock pulsation mode at 10-15 MHz frequency is identified across all cases despite a 24-fold variation in number density. In the wake, two distinct instabilities are observed. The canonical vortex shedding mode at Strouhal number St $\approx$ 0.2 dominates at lower Reynolds numbers. A second instability at St $\approx$ 0.5, consistent with previously reported slipline-driven oscillations in supersonic wakes, emerges at higher Reynolds numbers and progressively strengthens, becoming the dominant mode. In the studied Reynolds range, the wake transitions from no clear unsteadiness, to canonical vortex shedding at St $\approx$ 0.20, and reaching a regime where the St $\approx$ 0.5 mode becomes dominant, while also having a distinct independent bow shock pulsation possibly governed by its standoff distance.

papers.title: Identifying and disentangling direct and spillover effects using multiple pre-treatment periods
papers.abstract: Under interference, the treatment of some units affects the outcomes of others, so that the effect on a treated unit consists of a direct and a spillover component. A non-treated comparison group then generally identifies neither component, but the difference between the total effect on the treated and the spillover effect on the comparison units. Under certain identifying assumptions, both components may be identified separately when multiple pre-treatment periods are available, even in the absence of an uncontaminated comparison group. Under a no-anticipation assumption, pre-treatment outcomes are free of both components for every unit. Extrapolating the pre-treatment trend within a group, as in interrupted time-series approaches, therefore identifies the counterfactual outcome in the absence of any treatment, provided that the model used for the extrapolation is correctly specified. Applied to the treated it gives the total effect on them, applied to the non-treated at a given level of exposure the spillover effect on them. Disentangling the two components in addition requires effect homogeneity across treated and non-treated units with the same exposure and covariates, as well as common support in exposure. We derive doubly robust and Neyman-orthogonal expressions for the effects of interest, which permits controlling for possibly high-dimensional covariates by machine learning. A simulation study confirms the root-$n$ consistent behaviour of the estimators and the reliability of the standard errors under specific regularity conditions. We apply the framework to the compulsory licensing of enemy-owned patents in the United States in 1919. Licensing raised patenting in the licensed subclasses and in technologically close ones alike, so that a comparison-group design understates the total effect.

papers.title: Relative derived delooping levels and torsion intervals
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a support $τ$-tilting module over a finite dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq \text{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The heart $\mathcal H=\text{Fac} U\cap \mathcal{V}^\perp$ inherits the exact structure from mod$A$ and admits an Ext-progenerator $P$. Let $B=\text{End}_A(P)$. We define the relative derived delooping level on the exact heart $\mathcal H$ and compare it with the relative delooping level on $\mathcal {H}$ and the derived delooping level of $B$. We show that $\text{Findim} B^{op}$ is bounded by the relative derived delooping level on the $\mathcal H$. For a wide heart, the relative derived delooping level on the heart equals the derived delooping level of $B$. We obtain explicit bounds from representation-finite relative syzygy strata and characterize global first-order finiteness using an Ext-injective cogenerator.

papers.title: Higher-order strongly intensive observables for forward-backward multiplicity correlations
papers.abstract: Forward-backward multiplicity correlations probe the longitudinal structure of particle production, but fluctuations in the number of emitting sources complicate their interpretation. Strongly intensive observables remove the contribution of source-number fluctuations at second order. Here we extend the construction to all cumulant orders. For independent identical sources whose emission law does not depend on the source count, we build a normalized hierarchy of strongly intensive observables with $n$ new algebraically independent quantities at order $n$. Every observable is normalized to unity for statistically independent particles, vanishes when both window multiplicities are fixed, and remains finite at equal positive window means. We give explicit expressions through fourth order and an all-order recursion. Analytical particle production models and PYTHIA calculations for $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=0.9$ and 13 TeV demonstrate the sensitivity to window geometry, event selection, and connected multiparticle correlations. Fits constrained by the mean multiplicities and second-order observables provide conditional higher-order benchmarks. Deviations of these benchmarks from the PYTHIA results test the assumed correlation hierarchy, subject to the quality of the lower-order fit. Preliminary ALICE measurements at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV are used to illustrate the corresponding model-dependent scenarios.

papers.title: Self lensing in BH-NS binaries as progenitors for periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are bright extragalactic transients whose origin remains uncertain. The discovery of repeating FRBs, some with cyclic activity windows, opens new prospects for testing their progenitors. Neutron stars (NSs) are strong candidates, as they naturally emit radio pulses with temporal and spectral properties resembling those of FRBs, an interpretation reinforced by the detection of an FRB-like burst from the Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154. Nevertheless, the pulse energy of typical radio-emitting NSs remains several orders of magnitude below that of even the faintest observed FRBs. We explore a binary system in which a NS orbits a black hole (BH), so that NS radio pulses are gravitationally amplified through self-lensing, producing characteristic signatures in the energy distribution, activity windows, and waiting times that can be contrasted with observations. We implement a simple NS-BH binary model with a circular orbit undergoing Lense-Thirring precession, and compute how the pulses are lensed along the orbit, including pulse splitting and time delays. Pure Keplerian orbits produce activity windows several orders of magnitude shorter than those of periodic FRBs. Post-Keplerian orbits with Lense-Thirring precession are more promising, yielding windows of a few to tens of days. Lensing transforms an intrinsic log-normal NS pulse-energy distribution, producing a high-energy power-law tail spanning up to four orders of magnitude. Interpreting the observed millisecond waiting times between consecutive bursts as lensing-induced image delays, we infer BH masses of 10^3-10^4 solar masses, in the intermediate-mass (IMBH) range. However, the amplification in our model is insufficient to bridge the energy gap between Galactic magnetar radio pulses and FRBs. Moreover, the non-detection of NS-IMBH systems suggests a low abundance, so this channel is likely rare.

papers.title: A sparse canonical Rado theorem
papers.abstract: Canonical Ramsey theory studies structured colour patterns in colourings with arbitrarily many colours. Lefmann's canonical Rado theorem extends the canonical van der Waerden theorem of Erdős and Graham to partition-regular linear systems. Recently, Alvarado, Kohayakawa, Morris, Mota and Ortega proved a sparse canonical van der Waerden theorem for random set $[n]_p$. In this paper, we prove a sparse canonical Rado theorem. For every irredundant partition-regular matrix $A$ of positive rank with $k\ge3$ columns, and every prescribed partition witnessing the columns condition, if $p\ge Cn^{-1/m(A)}$, then with probability at least $1-e^{-cnp}$ every colouring of $[n]_p$ contains $$Ω\big(p^k n^{k-\rank(A)}\big)$$ canonical solutions of $A\mathbf x=0$ with distinct coordinates. A matching 0-statement holds when the prescribed partition has one or at least three blocks; the Schur equation shows that it can fail for two-block patterns. For every prescribed partition, we also establish a robust threshold at the same scale under deletion of a fixed positive proportion of the random set.

papers.title: Mapping Artistic Engagement with Quantum Technologies
papers.abstract: Quantum technologies (QT) are increasingly being taken up in artistic practices, for example in the form of visual artworks or quantum computer music. However, more comprehensive empirical studies on the temporal development and the different forms of QT-related art are still lacking. Therefore, this study conducted a systematic mapping and classification of QT-related artworks. To this end, a medium-independent corpus was established, and the artworks were classified into four categories: QT-Inspired, QT-Sourced, Simulated QT, and QT-Generated. This classification was LLM-assisted and checked against human-coded reference data as well as through manual review of unclear cases. In total, 281 QT-related artworks from 2010 to August 2025 were identified. The corpus shows a substantial increase in QT-related artworks since 2019, with a considerable share attributed to only a few artists. The different forms of QT relations coexist, while an increasing use of active hardware-based and simulated processes in artistic practices can be documented, particularly since 2021. Although no clear development trajectories between these categories can be identified, the observed development coincides with advances in QT and their improved accessibility. Thus, this study provides an empirical basis for further analyzing the development of QT-related art, the possible emergence of a "quantum art scene," and the reciprocal relationships between art and quantum technologies.

papers.title: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Audit-based certification bounds the violation rate of an LLM agent by auditing a random fraction $\varepsilon$ of actions and reweighting the audited labels; its validity is meant to rest only on the defender's audit coin. We show that it also rests on a confidentiality property: the coin must not interfere with the agent's view before the action commits, at a time the agent chooses. We call this pre-commit noninterference (PNI) and measure its violation by $D_{\mathrm{A}}$, the total-variation distance between the agent's views under the two coin values. PNI is necessary and sufficient for an unbiased certificate against adaptive agents, the worst-case bias is $(1-\varepsilon)D_{\mathrm{A}}$, and no procedure that sees only audited labels can pay less. Leakage composes across steps, a resource shared across episodes opens a channel of computable size, and raising the audit rate cannot restore validity. On a monitor we built, a silent audit changes no output but adds latency that tool timestamps expose, and the agent can enlarge it. A real LLM agent follows an injection that names a visible audit notice (generic, tool, and timing clauses have no effect); over that channel the plain certificate fails on measured labels and, by a post-hoc analysis, in a live run on a pre-registered schedule, while a silent audit restores it. A fresh coin per audited call closes the timing channel; padding only narrows it.

papers.title: Quantized Edge Inference of a Self-Supervised SAR-Optical Encoder on Commodity x86 Hardware
papers.abstract: Self-supervised vision transformers are increasingly used as reusable encoders for Earth observation, but their inference cost on the hardware available in the field is rarely characterized. We deploy a pretrained SAR-optical masked-autoencoder encoder on three commodity x86 nodes, from a low-power CPU without AVX2 to an AVX2+VNNI reference, at FP32, FP16 and INT8 on the CPU and, where present, the integrated GPU, and report latency, energy (RAPL and wall plug) and linear-probe accuracy. Quantization is accuracy-neutral: INT8 changes micro-mAP by only +0.0006, within the seed spread, so precision becomes a pure cost decision. INT8 lowers CPU latency on every node, by 1.45x even on the CPU without AVX2, and CPU energy wherever it is measured, and the VNNI reference (1.53x) suggests a further gain beyond AVX2. The Pareto-optimal device shifts from the integrated GPU, which is 4.38x faster than the CPU on the weakest node, to the CPU as the CPU class improves.

papers.title: Three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations
papers.abstract: We show that if a three-manifold $M$ admits a veering triangulation, then the dual spine of every essential triangulation of $M$ can be smoothed to a branched surface. We use this criterion to identify a large collection of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations. We then use the same criterion to construct the first infinite family of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds without veering triangulations.

papers.title: Exploring the Limits of the Delta Learning Hypothesis: Single-Pair Generator Biases in Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) typically relies on preference pairs generated from diverse model pools and ranked by an external LLM judge. The recently proposed delta-learning hypothesis suggests that comparable supervision can instead be obtained from a single pair of models by treating the larger model's response as preferred. We investigate the limits of this approach across model families and scales. We show, both theoretically and empirically, that fixed model pairs introduce systematic, generator-dependent biases that are predictive of the preference label independent of response quality. Consequently, DPO trained on single-pair data consistently underperforms multi-model preference data, despite the larger generator producing higher-quality responses, and we trace this gap to training dynamics consistent with reward hacking on these biases. We further show that simply increasing the number of generators, even without an external judge, is enough to partially mitigate this effect. Our results highlight generator diversity as a critical factor in preference-data construction.

papers.title: Jacob's ladders and wander from Hardy-Littlewood integral (1918) to the $ζ$-Platonic cube form of equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper we obtain $ζ$-Platonic cube form of our almost linear formula. From this follows, for example, the $ζ$-Platonic equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem. The last result represents the point of contact between the Hardy-Littlewood integral and the Fermat-Wiles theorem and also with one of the Platonic solid - cube.

papers.title: Janus Vehicles: Entity-Centric Threat Modelling of Protocol-Conformant Vehicles under a Malicious-Manufacturer Assumption
papers.abstract: Automotive cybersecurity commonly assumes benign end-product manufacturers and design authorities, focusing on supply-chain threats, external attacks, and compromised network participants observable through misbehaviour. This assumption overlooks malicious-by-design vehicles that remain authentic and protocol-conformant while performing undeclared sensing, communication, or context-triggered actuation. We formulate an Entity-Centric Threat Model spanning three subcomponents. The first, Malign Entity Archetypes, describes four types of malign entity: peer-benign, purpose-malicious vehicles; compromised vehicles; reappropriated genuine components; and imitated vehicles or components. The model exposes two assurance gaps: authenticity does not establish declared-purpose conformance, while malicious functionality can evade detection based on behavioural history or peer-visible evidence. Reappropriated components can remain genuine and retain usable identities or capabilities outside authorised contexts, reducing the effectiveness of signal fingerprinting and certificate-based authentication. To structure this threat space, we introduce a Behaviour-Locus Matrix that maps covert, overt, and concealment actions across hardware, software, and network loci. For peer-benign, purpose-malicious vehicles, we further present a Behavioural Interaction Model that represents how hidden capabilities are contextually activated, realised through actions, manifested within the vehicle and its environment, and potentially observed or concealed.

papers.title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
papers.abstract: This work proposes a hyper-reduced order model for coupled hydro-mechanical simulations of elastoplastic deformation and water flow in partially saturated soils. These simulations are used to monitor and assess the safety of geotechnical structures such as earthfill dams, where calibration, uncertainty quantification and scenario analysis require solving the same transient model many times for different parameter values. The displacement and the pore pressure are approximated in a field-split reduced basis obtained by proper orthogonal decomposition, and the Galerkin-projected equations are integrated with decomposed cubature rules, one per balance equation, built with the energy-conserving sampling and weighting (ECSW) method. Each residual is split into an affine part and a nonlinear correction: the affine part is computed exactly, at negligible online cost, so that the cubature rule only needs to approximate the correction, which is localized in space. The construction is independent of the constitutive model choices and is implemented in FEniCSx by assembling the original variational forms on the small set of elements selected by ECSW. The method is tested on two- and three-dimensional dams retaining tailings and water, simulating a raise of the dam and the subsequent consolidation phase, with the friction angle, stiffness and hydraulic conductivity of the dam material and the height of the raise as varying parameters. The hyper-reduced model reproduces the displacement and pressure fields with errors below $0.5\%$ with respect to the finite element solution, achieving speed-ups of up to $43\times$ in two dimensions and $77\times$ in three. These performance gains grow with the extent of the plastic yielding, and the selected elements concentrate in the plastified and unsaturated zones, whose size is set by the physics rather than by the mesh resolution.

papers.title: GKS Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Security Analysis
papers.abstract: All traditional encryption schemes share a fundamental operational vulnerability: encrypted data must be decrypted before it can be used. Fully homomorphic encryption eliminates this vulnerability by enabling computation directly on encrypted data, but existing FHE schemes impose substantial practical constraints that limit deployment. This paper presents a formal security analysis of the Gribov-Kahrobaei-Shpilrain (GKS) private-key FHE scheme. GKS requires no bootstrapping or de-linearization, produces bit-exact decryption, supports native encrypted search, and scales to unbounded depth.

papers.title: EnergyCal: Taming Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training
papers.abstract: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language-model training can exhibit large loss spikes with Muon-family optimizers. We introduce EnergyCal, a lightweight rule that attenuates routed-expert updates according to the normalized squared Frobenius norm of their finite-step Newton-Schulz directions. EnergyCal leaves the spectral transform unchanged and adds no persistent optimizer state. We evaluate it on a 4B-parameter MoE model. Against a development-selected, lower-learning-rate MuonH recipe, EnergyCal-MuonH reduces mean thresholded loss-spike burden by 99.51% and final geometric-mean perplexity by 4.06%, with a modest throughput cost. With plain Muon at matched nominal learning rate and weight decay, the reduction in mean spike burden averages 95.98% across the two tested exponents, accompanied by small endpoint improvements. These findings support stabilization both with and without Hyperball in the evaluated setting.

papers.title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact Kähler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation. Even for a smooth hypertoric manifold, a reducible core forces every cut in the outer cut chamber to have non-trivial cyclic isotropy, while the cuts are smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety, which is then a product of projective spaces. For a positive regular integral level $d$ in the outer cut chamber, algebraic cutting identifies the cut's quantisation with a finite filtration piece of the circle-graded quantisation of the original hypertoric variety, whose successive quotients recover the individual circle-weight spaces. We prove that the higher cohomology of the pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes at every such level, so that the localised index is the character of the actual space of sections. Finally, a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the arrangement slack function, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. Thus, each finite stage admits a weighted lattice-point description whose multiplicity function is supported on the lattice points in the support of the level-$d$ moment polyptych.

papers.title: Genesis in Minimally Modified Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct a Genesis scenario within the framework of a type-II minimally modified gravity. The background solution is past geodesically complete and approaches Minkowski spacetime in the asymptotic past. While the Hubble expansion rate grows, the matter sector satisfies the null-energy condition. Scalar perturbations are ghost-free and have no ultraviolet gradient instability, although the squared sound speed $c_\mathcal{R}^2$ becomes negative within a finite infrared region in the Fourier space for a finite time interval. Numerical evolution, including superhorizon growth, yields a nearly scale-invariant, slightly red-tilted scalar spectrum over a broad region of parameter space. The tensor spectrum is blue, with a strongly suppressed tensor-to-scalar ratio. Finally, using the matter fluctuation $δχ$, whose asymptotic normalization is regular, we find that the background-dependent cubic couplings vanish in the far past at fixed nonzero momenta. The surviving matter--graviton and graviton self-interactions are Planck suppressed.

papers.title: Scattering amplitudes from geometry of kernel-free functionals on piecewise random null paths with memory
papers.abstract: We introduce a simple functional of algebra-valued fields with definite Lorentz properties that is kernel-free yet it encodes the structure of tree-level scattering amplitudes. The fields are evaluated at the points of a piece-wise straight paths in the anti-self-dual plane of complexified Minkowski space, with the directions of consecutive segments correlated so that the path has a velocity memory. We show that momentum-space reduction of the functional generates the cyclic Parke--Taylor factor, off shell in terms of light-front bilinears and on shell in terms of spinor brackets. The same reduction, organized differently, can be naturally promoted to twistor space without any twistor-space input: a closed cyclic chain of Penrose transforms on a twistor line, in which the Parke--Taylor denominators arise as boundary terms of the integrals along the paths. Finally we show that derivatives with respect to one of the path parameter generate numerators that together with the Parke-Taylor denominator build scattering amplitudes. Lorentz invariance fixes the spins of the inserted fields and the homogeneities of the corresponding twistor functions without any use of supersymmetry. The three-point outputs reproduce the kinematic forms of the light-cone cubic vertices of chiral higher-spin theory, and the derivative monomials of order four generate the components of the $\overline{\rm MHV}$ supermultiplet of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory, off shell and on shell.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Mixed Evacuation Problem
papers.abstract: The mixed evacuation problem is a variant of the dynamic transshipment problem where there exist two modes of transportation and we allocate supplies to each mode of transportation in such a way that we can send all the supplies from sources to sinks within a given time limit. It is known that this problem can be solved in polynomial time when the number of sources and sinks is small. In this paper, we prove that the mixed evacuation problem can be solved in polynomial time with the ellipsoid method.

papers.title: Improved Brunn--Minkowski inequality for $θ$-convolution bodies
papers.abstract: For $n\geq 2$, we study the optimal function $\varphi_n$ in the Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $θ$-convolution bodies $|K+_θL|^{1/n}\geq\varphi_n(θ)(|K|^{1/n}+|L|^{1/n})$ for any convex bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$. We improve the known lower bound for every $0<θ<(3/4)^n$ and determine $\varphi_n$ on an interval strictly containing $[(2/3)^n,1]$. For $θ<1$ in this interval, equality holds if and only if $K$ and $-L$ are translates of the same $n$-dimensional simplex. The proof reduces the geometric problem to a sharp one-dimensional estimate for nonnegative concave functions under a weighted integral constraint.

papers.title: Placing the Beamspace Window on a Hopping Carrier: Bin Drift, Exact Capture and the Cost of Rounding
papers.abstract: A frequency-agile radar with a large digital array moves the spatial frequency of its look direction across the beams of a spatial FFT every time it changes carrier, so a beamspace adaptive processor must decide where to put its window at each hop. Because the beamspace transform is orthonormal, the output of the processor depends only on the span of the window, and a hop changes nothing but where the window sits. Centring the window exactly on the fractional bin of the look direction keeps the look vector fully inside it at every carrier, for the price of one phase ramp before the FFT. On a 32 by 32 array over 4 to 8 GHz the look bin drifts by 1.6 to 6.9 bins for look directions from u=0.2 to 60 degrees. Rounding to the nearest bin costs up to 1.34, 0.74 and 0.50 dB of look-direction capture for 3 by 3, 5 by 5 and 7 by 7 windows. In a three-jammer scenario with 41 carriers, a window frozen at the lowest carrier loses 39 to 60 dB at the worst carrier for a look direction of u=0.55, the exact window beats nearest-bin placement by 0.31 to 0.65 dB there, and the advantage reverses for a nine-beam window near broadside, where nearest-bin was 0.61 dB better.

papers.title: Hierarchical Low-Rank Reparameterization for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods adapt large models by introducing a small number of trainable parameters. However, we find that these parameters still contain redundancy and can be further compressed while maintaining strong task performance. To this end, we propose a novel hierarchical low-rank reparameterization method. Its core idea is to reorganize the trainable parameters of PEFT methods into an approximately square matrix and then express it via a low-rank decomposition, which can be applied recursively. This forms a multi-level structure with factors compressed level by level, drastically reducing the number of trainable parameters. In our experiments, we combine this reparameterization with LoRA, DoRA, MoSA, and RaSA. We evaluate commonsense reasoning on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, with additional GSM8K math reasoning experiments on LLaMA-3.1-8B. Under comparable trainable-parameter budgets, our method combined with LoRA or DoRA achieves better performance. Furthermore,when the parameter count of the original methods is compressed by approximately an order of magnitude, our method can still maintain competitive task performance and even surpass the corresponding baselines in average accuracy across the eight commonsense reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: Observer-Based Event-Triggered Control of Infinite-Dimensional Linear Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate observer-based event-triggered stabilization of infinite-dimensional linear systems, such as those governed by partial differential equations. A Luenberger observer and a feedback gain are assumed to stabilize the closed loop in continuous time, and we study what happens when the control input is only updated at instants generated by a dynamic event-triggering mechanism. Unlike approaches that rely on state-dependent triggering rules, our condition only involves the observer state and the measured output, which makes it implementable when the full state is not measured. It compares the deviation of a monitored signal of the observer since the last update with a threshold made of two parts. The first one is a relative part, proportional to the current size of this signal, and the second one is a positive internal variable, which does not depend on the observer state. In particular, the case where the threshold reduces to the internal variable alone is covered. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the well-posedness of the closed-loop system and the absence of Zeno behavior for general choices of these two parts, and we prove its exponential stability under a small-gain condition on the relative part. We further analyse the existence of a dwell-time, namely a positive lower bound on the time elapsed between two consecutive triggering instants. When the sampled dynamics is bounded, as in finite-dimensional systems or systems with a finite-dimensional unstable part, we obtain a dwell-time independent of the initial data, together with exponential stability. For unbounded generators, we exhibit a system satisfying all our assumptions for which no triggering rule can achieve both a dwell-time independent of the initial data and bounded trajectories.

papers.title: Correctness Conditioning as Selection in Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Evaluation
papers.abstract: Restricting chain-of-thought (CoT) faithfulness evaluation to correctly answered instances changes the population being measured. We study this selection step in a seven-variable structural causal model and derive the exact observed gap $Δ= \operatorname{Cov}(A, C)/P(C=1)$. The model distinguishes difficulty confounding from shortcut-induced collider bias and states the conditional-independence assumption needed to express the gap through latent response propensities. A protocol review of 18 papers distinguishes answer-correctness restrictions from agreement-based selection, benchmark construction, and training-data filtering. We evaluate four sub-ceiling deployments on arithmetic tasks and observe positive selection gaps in all four. The primary GLM-5.3 run yields a +7.4 percentage-point gap ($n = 1000$, $p < 0.0001$), and pooled Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel analysis gives OR = 1.70 ($p < 10^{-6}$). An assumption-free covariance decomposition assigns 42.8% of the GLM-5.3 gap to between-stratum variation in interventionable-operation count, leaving the majority unattributed. When counterfactual compliance is observable for every instance, evaluating all traces directly estimates population faithfulness without correctness filtering.

papers.title: Analysis of Uncertain GARCH Model with the application of crude oil future prices
papers.abstract: Time series data often exhibit variation, clustering, and persistence in uncertain environments. Based on an uncertain measure, existing studies have primarily focused on conditional mean structures while ignoring variance and persistent dynamics. To address this gap, this paper develops an uncertain generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (UGARCH) model that incorporates lagged conditional variance terms. We first prove sufficient conditions to ensure mean stationarity of the variance process. Then, we propose recursive constrained least squares to estimate the model parameters and use cross validation to determine the orders of the mean and variance equations. In addition, we also employ uncertain hypothesis tests to determine whether a time series exhibits a UGARCH effect and to assess the goodness of fit. Point and interval forecasts are subsequently constructed from the recursively obtained next-period conditional variance and the expected value of the mean equation. Numerical simulations demonstrate the parameter estimation performance of the proposed method and show that UGARCH achieves smaller conditional-variance fitting errors than UARCH under the considered settings. In the empirical analysis, we apply the proposed method to West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures closing prices, which exhibit time-varying volatility and support short-term point and interval forecasts. Keywords: Uncertain measure, Uncertain time-series analysis, UGARCH model, hypothesis test

papers.title: Two Exceptional-Point Regimes in the Spinterface Model of Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
papers.abstract: The spinterface model of chirality-induced spin selectivity supports two algebraically distinct near-exceptional-point (EP) regimes, which cannot be mixed. A \emph{gold-level} near-EP involves the two gold spin states under an anti-Hermitian, electrode-mediated spin flip with spin-symmetric dissipative broadening (Scheme~B). A \emph{chain-level} near-EP involves the collective coalescence of the two molecular eigenstates with largest weight on the first molecular site under a Hermitian on-site Rashba spin flip with spin-dependent broadening (Scheme~A). Mixing the diagonal cancellation of one scheme with the off-diagonal structure of the other yields a strictly negative discriminant and admits no EP on any parameter path, making the gold/chain classification exhaustive. At the gold near-EP the spin-flip coupling is chirality-selective, converting achiral spin-valve transport into purely chiral transport across well-defined crossover points. At the chain near-EP the Petermann factor grows as a power law in chain length, with an exponent tunable by the Rashba coherence length and non-monotonic in the Rashba strength, reflecting a balance between coherent enhancement and progressive breakdown of the Scheme-A condition. Both near-EPs are dressed versions of the ideal two-state EP, and the ratio between observed and bare EP locations measures the delocalisation of the coalescing pair, providing a fit-free diagnostic of the mechanism. These results identify CISS junctions as a solid-state platform for non-Hermitian spectral physics.

papers.title: Settlement percolation reveals shrinking critical distances across the urban hierarchy
papers.abstract: Measures of urban expansion quantify land consumption but obscure how separated settlements coalesce. We examine India's 50 largest urban agglomerations (1975-2025) using percolation-like analysis. Critical distances marking the largest settlement-merger events contracted in 47 cities, the median falling 46% from 650 to 350m. This longitudinal shrinking of settlement connectivity length scales reveals a morphological mechanism shaping land-consumptive settlement growth through distinct forms of inter-cluster coalescence (compact, corridor, satellite, regional). Population size shows no detectable linear relationship with contraction magnitude, although intermediate-sized agglomerations display the widest observed spread. Confirming established land-consumption patterns, built-up surfaces and urban footprints grow faster than population. Yet their relative growth flips with urban delineation: before the largest merger, footprints outgrow built-up surface (386% versus 361%); immediately afterward, built-up surface outgrows footprints (315% versus 287%). Recognizing merger dynamics can guide infrastructure investment, prioritize sustainable infill, reduce land consumption, and protect agricultural and ecologically sensitive landscapes.

papers.title: Systematic Morphometric Brain Autoencoding for Representation Learning in Neurodegenerative Diseases
papers.abstract: Early identification of neurodegenerative disorders using structural T1-weighted MRI is essential for timely clinical intervention, yet supervised deep learning models often struggle to generalize due to limited annotations and scanner-induced distribution shift. Self-supervised learning offers a promising alternative; however, existing approaches are largely adapted from natural image paradigms, relying on contrastive objectives or generic masked reconstruction with voxel-wise losses, which may not fully capture the distributed morphometric patterns associated with neurodegeneration. We introduce SYMBA (SYstematic Morphometric Brain Autoencoding), a self-supervised pretraining framework specifically designed for structural brain MRI. SYMBA integrates anatomically constrained masking, a multi-scale structural similarity (MS-SSIM) reconstruction objective, and a progressive curriculum that transitions from local anatomical detail to global brain morphology. These components explicitly incorporate neuroanatomical structure into the self-supervised objective rather than relying on generic image priors. Pretrained on 6,953 T1-weighted MRI scans from nine heterogeneous cohorts, SYMBA is evaluated using frozen linear probing on two independent unseen datasets, enabling a strict assessment of out-of-distribution generalization. Across multiple clinical tasks, SYMBA consistently outperforms recent neuroimaging foundation models, achieving 0.930 AUROC for Alzheimer's disease classification, 0.772 for mild cognitive impairment conversion prediction, and strong performance in amyloid status prediction. In low-label regimes, SYMBA demonstrates high sample efficiency, reaching approximately 0.90 AUROC for AD/CN classification using only six labeled subjects.

papers.title: All Strict Calabi--Yau Threefolds of Height One Lift to Characteristic 0
papers.abstract: We prove that every strict Calabi--Yau threefold of Artin--Mazur height one over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 admits a projective lift to W(k). No assumption is made on the torsion in its crystalline cohomology, and p is arbitrary. Using the crystalline period map of Brantner and Taelman, we show that the obstruction to extending a lift over W_n(k) is the Bockstein of a torsion coordinate of its period point, and that this coordinate can always be made to vanish by varying the lift. The mixed-characteristic deformation functor need not be smooth: for a Calabi--Yau threefold of height one constructed by Addington and Bragg in characteristic 3, some lifts over W_2(k) do not extend over W_3(k). This disproves a conjecture of Achinger and Zdanowicz.

papers.title: Perimeter shell properties of branched polymer adsorbents in various conformational states
papers.abstract: The structural accessibility and perimeter shell properties of branched macromolecules are studied using Monte Carlo simulations on a simple cubic lattice. Constituent polymer chains of these macromolecules are constructed in an algorithmic way as: a set of collinear monomers; a self-avoiding walk (SAW); tigthly packed monomers. These mimic the ground states for a rigid rod, flexible chain, and collapsed chain conformational states, respectively. We analyzed the set of observables that are related to adsorption, such as perimeter shell size (number of available sites for particle adsorption) per monomer $\langle \bar{n}_a \rangle$, mean coordination number of perimeter shell $\langle n_{\rm bond} \rangle$ (average number of contacts per adsorbed particle), and coordination accessibility per monomer $\langle \bar{n}_s \rangle$. Our results demonstrate that branching reduces the perimeter shell size while it increases mean coordination number of perimeter shell across all conformational states, due to higher local monomer density near branching cores and formation of shared adsorption sites or microcages. Stiff extended structures yield the highest values for $\langle \bar{n}_a \rangle$ (approaching $4$ in the limit of long chains), whereas the flexible ones provide the largest values for $\langle n_{\rm bond} \rangle$. We can note that the collinearity of monomers in constituent chains works in the same direction as reduction of branching ($\langle \bar{n}_a \rangle$ grows), whereas the { tight packing of them} -- in the same direction as the increase of branching ($\langle \bar{n}_a \rangle$ decreases)

papers.title: The NWU ageing property of the gamma-gamma distribution
papers.abstract: Baricz et al. [BPV2011] posed the question of whether the $K$-distribution (or gamma-gamma distribution) satisfies the ageing property known as the new is better than used (NBU) property. In this paper we address this question by establishing that, under certain parameter conditions, the gamma-gamma distribution satisfies the new is worse than used (NWU) property rather than the NBU property. For the remaining parameter ranges, we show that the gamma-gamma distribution is neither NBU nor NWU. The proofs rely on tools from the theory of stochastic orders of random variables. Moreover, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the $K$-distribution is actually the product of two independent gamma random variables, we obtain alternative proofs of our results. Similarly, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the beta-prime distribution is actually the quotient of two independent gamma random variables, we establish analogous NBU/NWU properties for this distribution. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the product of two independent positive random variables possesses the NWU and decreasing failure rate (DFR) properties. On the other hand, we show that the survival function of the $K$-distribution is hyperbolically completely monotone by representing it as the Laplace transform of a random variable belonging to the class of generalized gamma convolutions. As a consequence, we establish some monotonicity properties of the Mills ratio and hazard rate function of the $K$-distribution. These results provide further insight into the ageing and monotonicity properties of the gamma-gamma distribution. In addition, we derive a new integral representation and two new series representations, as well as bounds, for the survival function of the $K$-distribution.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and scattering of energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness and scattering for the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} i\partial_t u + Δu = |u|^{\frac{4}{d-2}} u, u(0) = u_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} on hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d(d \geq 4)$. We mainly utilize the concentration-compactness/rigidity method. We establish a linear profile decomposition on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces and prove that the nonlinear profile on hyperbolic spaces can be approximated by the solutions of the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on Euclidean spaces, then obtaining the global well-posedness and scattering of the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the high-dimensional hyperbolic space.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness and Large Time Asymptotic Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Compressible Viscous Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Vacuum
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem to the compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system in $\mathbb{R}^3$, in which the velocity is planar while the magnetic field is vertical. For regular initial data with small energy but possibly large oscillations, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solution with vacuum. In addition, the large-time behavior of the solution is investigated. A key ingredient is an application of the Bourgain--Brezis divergence estimate to handle the total pressure $ρ^γ+m^2$ for any adiabatic index $γ>1$. This enables us to control both components of the total pressure, $ρ^γ$ and $m^2$, by a single estimate that remains valid in the presence of vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, our result is the first one on global solvability to the compressible, viscous, non-resistive MHD system in the special 2$\frac12$-dimensional whole space allowing vacuum.
