papers.title: Orthogonal Zadoff-Chu Based Pilot Design For Fractional Channel Estimation in MIMO-OTFS
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence-based pilot design for fractional channel estimation in orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation for point-to-point multi-input multi-output (MIMO) scenarios. Orthogonal pilot sequences are assigned to each transmit antenna using ZF sequences. At the receiver, a correlation-based scheme is used to construct the signal for estimation. The estimation relies on a two-dimensional extension of the Aboutanios and Mulgrew (A&M) frequency estimation method. Simulation results show that the proposed approach achieves low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) while maintaining stable performance as the number of transmit antennas increases.

papers.title: Tessera: Structure-Completed Evidence Units for Web Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Web retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) splits a page into fixed-size text chunks or, in recent visual pipelines, screenshot tiles, and the retrieved item serves at once as the unit of indexing, ranking, and reading. We trace answer evidence from source HTML to reader input over the full English Wikipedia and find that this coupling loses evidence in text and screenshot pipelines alike: evidence present in the source page often fails to reach the reader intact, particularly structured content such as tables and infoboxes, which chunking separates from the headers and context that give it meaning. Stronger extraction, context expansion, and larger reader budgets leave the loss in place. We present Tessera, a training-free evidence delivery layer that decouples what a pipeline retrieves from what its reader reads. Given the pages behind any ranked list, Tessera rebuilds their HTML into fine-grained evidence units, each completed with its page title, section path, and table headers, selects the units relevant to the query, and packs them into the reader context at an unchanged token budget. The index, the retriever, and the reader stay as they are, so Tessera applies to text, screenshot, and agentic pipelines. Across three question answering benchmarks, Tessera improves answer accuracy by 5 to 6 points on text and screenshot pipelines, consistently across readers, retrievers, and reader budgets, and outperforms strong HTML-aware and structure-aware RAG baselines under matched budgets. The gains carry over to multi-step agentic search. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/sarendis56/Tessera.

papers.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
papers.abstract: Background and purpose: Radiotherapy planning agents based on large language models (LLMs) decide when to submit a plan or request review but are evaluated mainly by dose. This study developed OpenGray, a benchmark of planning tasks with known correct decisions. Materials and methods: OpenGray adds tasks with known answers to the OpenKBP-Opt head-and-neck dataset, including two contradictions with dose goals proven incompatible and a feasible control with a stored plan meeting every hard goal. Four systems, from a rule-based planning script to a full LLM agent, were evaluated on 30 patients, the LLM-based ones with a commercial (Terra) and a local (Ministral 3 8B) LLM. Decisions, achieved dose, problem recognition, and technical failures were recorded and also read from logs of 39 stereotactic radiosurgery runs of SAGE, a clinical LLM agent. Results: With Terra, the script preceded by an LLM review and the full agent had decision accuracies of 95.4% and 92.1%, respectively, yet escalated only 50% (95% confidence interval, 25-75%) and 25% (10-40%) of overlap contradictions, which required arithmetic on the anatomy. All four systems submitted every feasible control, but 24% of these plans missed a hard goal that the stored plan had met. In four SAGE runs, one goal failed at every attempt; the agent identified it in every reply but had no action for stopping. Conclusions: Favorable aggregate scores concealed specific decision failures. Planning agents should be evaluated on their decisions as well as their dose and given an explicit action for stopping and requesting review.

papers.title: Reducing Complexity of Pseudo-Marginal Sequential Monte Carlo via Hierarchical Tempering
papers.abstract: The Bayesian approach to inverse problems provides a powerful framework for inferring unknown parameters from noisy observations. Among the computationally most challenging statistical inference problems are problems with intractable likelihoods, especially if no unbiased likelihood estimator is available. We focus on a class of such problems, where a biased likelihood estimator is obtained through a stochastic approximation of a forward map (stochastic solver). Obtaining an empirical posterior approximation in applications is very expensive due to the repeated stochastic solver evaluations required by standard sampling methods. To address this computational bottleneck, we develop a novel algorithm based on a density-tempered marginalized Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) sampler. Our approach (hierarchical SMC) accelerates inference by leveraging a hierarchy of stochastic solvers with increasing accuracy both along the tempering sequence and within mutation stages of the SMC sampler. We establish, under additional assumptions, that the asymptotic speedup is proportional to the number of tempering stages $T$. We demonstrate computational gains on several examples, including a nonlinear, high-contrast inverse problem arising in photoacoustic medical imaging. On this problem, we demonstrate a speedup by a factor of 14.3, reducing the inference wall-clock time from about 4.6 days to 7.7 hours on an NVIDIA A40 GPU.

papers.title: Design and Architecture of Airmod: An Active Noise Cancellation and Deep Learning System for Real-Time Respiratory Rate Estimation from Tracheal Sounds
papers.abstract: Tracheal auscultation is recommended by clinical practice guidelines, and required by some U.S. state regulations, for monitoring ventilation during procedural sedation and monitored anesthesia care. However, continuous auscultation with a conventional stethoscope is impractical, susceptible to ambient noise, and difficult to interpret. We developed the Artificial Intelligence Respiratory MOnitoring Device (Airmod), an FDA-cleared software as a medical device (510(k) K242798) that continuously monitors tracheal sounds and estimates breath-to-breath respiratory rate in real time. In this paper, we describe its software architecture and key processing modules. Ambient noise is suppressed by active noise control, using a normalized least-mean-square adaptive filter with a dual-microphone electronic stethoscope. A multiclass convolutional bidirectional gated recurrent unit (CNN-BiGRU) model detects inhalations and exhalations in 15-s inference windows. It was trained on HF_Tracheal_V2, a new database of 373 continuous tracheal sound recordings (8,521 min; 107,644 labeled inhalations) from 369 subjects under sedation. To handle continuous acoustic streaming, Airmod runs inference on overlapping 15-s windows. It refines the detected inhalations by removing incomplete events, low-energy false positives, and double counts, concatenates them into a history list, and estimates respiratory rate from the mean period of the last three breaths. On the test set, at the default 2-s prediction interval with refinement enabled, inhalation detection achieved a sensitivity of 0.828, a positive predictive value of 0.832, and an F1-score of 0.830. Airmod also broadcasts the noise-cancelled tracheal sound and displays a real-time spectrogram to help clinicians recognize respiratory abnormalities.

papers.title: Approximation of the Narrowband Velocity Ambiguity Function in Near-Field Sensing Systems
papers.abstract: This work investigates the velocity ambiguity function in the radiative near-field of a uniform linear antenna array. First, the general ambiguity function is formulated and the velocity cross-section at a target position is considered. The velocity vector is decomposed into radial and tangential components, which are analyzed separately. Next, the closed-form approximations for the velocity ambiguity function are derived and shown to be accurate despite relying on far-field approximations. The results show that the near-field regime does not improve radial velocity estimation, but enables estimation of the tangential velocity. Finally, the velocity ambiguity functions and the achievable resolution are analyzed for different array configurations. For tangential velocity estimation, MIMO and a collection of SISO radars offer improved ambiguity function and resolution as compared to the SIMO/MISO configuration.

papers.title: On the Sparsity of Direct Preference Optimization: Weight Disentanglement in the NTK Regime
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has been widely adopted for aligning language models with human preferences. Recent empirical work has revealed that DPO induces remarkably sparse parameter updates, yet no theoretical explanation for this phenomenon has been offered. We analyze DPO's optimization dynamics under a neural tangent kernel linearization and show that the logistic structure of the DPO loss gives rise to an implicit maximum-margin bias. Building on this observation, we introduce the concept of dual sparsity: the DPO update direction is a sparse linear combination (data-level sparsity, driven by support vectors) of sparse gradient feature vectors (parameter-level sparsity, arising from gradient cancellation between preferred and dispreferred responses). We formalize this structure in our main theorem, bound the number of support pairs by a margin-dependent spectral quantity, and present a framework relating dual sparsity to weight disentanglement---a condition favorable for model merging. Experiments on GPT-2 Small and Medium and on 7--9B instruction-tuned models (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B) with the Anthropic HH-RLHF and UltraFeedback datasets confirm both sources of sparsity, and experiments on GPT-2 show that DPO reduces cross-task interference by up to $35{\times}$ compared to supervised fine-tuning.

papers.title: Is Your LLM Relay Serving What It Claims? A low-cost and high-power test for LLM Relay Auditing
papers.abstract: Relay and reseller APIs have become a common way to access large language models (LLMs), yet users cannot directly verify whether they receive the models they request and pay for. This opacity motivates LLM relay auditing, but existing methods struggle to combine low cost, robustness to benign deployment changes, and statistically interpretable decisions under black-box access. To address these limitations, we propose distributional fingerprint auditing (DFA), a statistical method that requires only textual responses from suspect and trusted reference endpoints. DFA repeatedly queries semantically simple finite-choice probes and uses the resulting categorical response distributions to construct endpoint fingerprints. It compares the suspect and reference fingerprints probe by probe and aggregates the resulting evidence using the Cauchy combination test, yielding an approximate endpoint-level $p$-value for audit decisions at a prespecified nominal significance level. Using registered fingerprints of candidate models, a likelihood-based formulation further supports model attribution under full substitution and joint estimation of substitute identity and substitution ratio under constant-ratio mixed routing. Our benchmark includes 16 proprietary and open-weight LLMs from 10 model families. Across 240 ordered full-substitution pairs, DFA achieves high detection rates at a nominal significance level of $α=0.05$, using five probes and 250 relay requests per audit with stored reference fingerprints. Configuration overrides can lead to rejection even when the served model remains unchanged, with effects varying across models and configurations. Simulations based on stored empirical fingerprints demonstrate accurate model attribution and estimate substitution ratios, with estimation error decreasing as the audit budget increases.

papers.title: Exact decoherence dynamics of a detector coupled to vacuum fluctuations in bounded geometries
papers.abstract: The properties of quantum vacuum are highly sensitive to the underlying spacetime geometry and boundary conditions. We investigate in this paper the decoherence dynamics of a two-level system (detector) coupled to a vacuum scalar field through the $\hatσ_z$-coupling scheme under various boundary environments. By rigorously evaluating the reduced density matrix of the detector, we derive an exact general expression for the detector's decoherence function, $γ(Δt)$, and use it to characterize the dynamical decoherence of a detector in three scenarios: free space, a perfectly reflecting boundary, and a cavity formed by two parallel reflecting boundaries. We find that in free space the detector's coherence decays monotonically with time, indicating that vacuum fluctuations alone inevitably lead to a complete loss of coherence. In the single-boundary case, by contrast, the detector's coherence displays non-monotonic time evolution: $γ(Δt)$ increases with time up to a maximum and then settles to a steady value, indicating that the initial coherence can be partially preserved due to the presence of the boundary. When the detector is placed inside a cavity, its coherence evolution exhibits oscillatory behavior, and a significant fraction of the initial coherence survives. Moreover, for the same detector-boundary distance, more coherence is preserved in the cavity case than in the single-boundary case. These results provide a viable route for engineering quantum coherence via boundary conditions.

papers.title: Systematic calculations of β-delayed fission probabilities using a microscopic framework
papers.abstract: The process of $β$-delayed fission ($β$DF) consists of a mother nucleus $β$-decaying to different states of a daughter isotope, followed by fission of the latter with a probability that strongly depends on the energy of the states populated in the $β$ decay. Studying this process experimentally can be challenging due to the typically small $β$DF probabilities. The theoretical framework presented in this work was developed to globally characterise $β$DF probabilities. This approach uses energy density functional based models to obtain the necessary inputs for the final probabilities, which are obtained through the nuclear reaction code TALYS. Calculations were performed for all isotopes with an experimentally measured value of $β$DF probabilities. Following the optimisation of the theoretical framework to better reproduce known data, a global RMS deviation of about two orders of magnitude was achieved, an accuracy that can be used to identify promising cases for future experimental $β$DF studies.

papers.title: Closed-Form Subspace Loss and Snapshot-Limited Dimension Selection for Beamspace MVDR Radar
papers.abstract: A beamspace minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) processor adapts a window of B beams instead of all N elements of a large array, trading a subspace loss that falls with B against a covariance estimation loss that rises with B for a fixed number K of training snapshots. We give the subspace loss of a DFT beam window in point jamming in closed form: exactly for any jammer power, and in the high interference-to-noise ratio (INR) limit through the Dirichlet kernel of the array. Combined with the known scaled-Beta law of sample matrix inversion (SMI) with a fixed transform, it gives a window size B*(K) for unloaded SMI. On a simulated 32x32 array with carriers from 4 to 8 GHz, noise jammers and Billingsley land clutter, the exact form is within 0.04 dB of the clairvoyant subspace loss for 25- and 49-beam windows at jammer levels from 10 to 50 dB. For a 9-beam window whose three columns are taken by three jammers near the target's elevation, the clutter that the form leaves out costs up to 5 dB. With the nominal K, B*(K) picks the lowest-loss window in all 30 cases with more than one runnable window. The rule is an oracle: it needs the jammer parameters or the true covariance, and errors of 0.25 bin rms in the jammer directions add a mean loss of 0.04 dB. With diagonal loading the best window was larger still wherever the rule chose more than the smallest window.

papers.title: Transport statistics in asymmetric coupled chaotic dots in series: Brownian motion model
papers.abstract: We study statistics of transport properties in a system of two quantum chaotic cavities coupled in series through a tunable junction and connected to reservoirs with asymmetric leads. Within the random matrix theory framework and in the absence of time-reversal symmetry, the scattering matrix S undergoes a crossover from two independent circular unitary ensembles to a single CUE as the inter-cavity coupling increases. Modeling this crossover using Dyson's Brownian motion approach, with the junction width acting as a time-like parameter, we derive closed-form expressions for the time-dependent averages and variances of conductance and shot noise power for arbitrary lead asymmetry. These analytical results reduce to known expressions in the symmetric and fully coupled limits. The mapping between the Brownian time parameter and the physical junction width is found to be observable-dependent, reflecting the different eigenfunction correlations probed by conductance and shot noise power, and this dependence is examined and separately calibrated for each observable. Validating against random-matrix simulations and tight-binding transport calculations using Kwant, we find quantitative agreement for ensemble-averaged observables throughout the crossover, while variances, being more sensitive to microscopic fluctuations, show deviations from the Brownian-motion predictions.

papers.title: GAWM: A Compact Latent World-Action Model for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) incorporate the prediction of future observations into robot policy learning. However, most WAMs build on billion-parameter vision-language or video-generation backbones, which incur high training cost and inference latency. In this letter, we present GAWM (Geometry-Aware World Model), a compact multi-task WAM that predicts future observations in the latent space of a frozen DINOv3 encoder. GAWM compresses the features of each camera view into a small set of tokens. A lightweight predictor, conditioned on the task rather than on actions, forecasts these tokens at two future horizons. The forecast is supervised with the dense patch features of future frames, which requires it to encode the spatial layout of the future scene. An action decoder directly regresses a chunk of future actions from the current and predicted tokens. With fewer than 100M parameters and no robot or video pretraining, GAWM outperforms billion-parameter WAMs on RoboTwin 2.0 and performs comparably to billion-parameter VLAs on LIBERO. On a dual-arm robot, it achieves lower action-prediction error on held-out demonstrations than a fine-tuned billion-parameter VLA, with substantially lower inference latency. Ablation studies show that the latent world model substantially improves performance when training data or training time is limited. Code is available at https://github.com/gaoxiang12/ga-wm.

papers.title: Quantum Fisher Information Deficit as a Geometric Signature of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: Recently, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) has been established as a framework for describing quantum phases in open systems. However SW-SSB cannot be characterized by conventional charged two-point correlators. In this work, we show that, for strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions, SW-SSB manifests as a persistent deficit from the maximal quantum Fisher information (QFI) under symmetry-neutral pair rotations. A model-independent inequality hierarchy establishes the equivalence of this deficit with fidelity and Rényi-1 correlators as asymptotic long-range-order diagnostics. It thereby connects finite-angle state overlaps to a constraint on the infinitesimal Bures geometry along the same pair-generated orbit. For symmetry-projected Gibbs states, we further derive a lower bound on the deficit governed by the mean energy injected by the pair operation. Crucially, locality keeps this energy cost uniformly bounded in system size and endpoint separation, maintaining a finite gap below the maximal QFI at any fixed finite temperature. When ordinary charged long range order is absent, this persistent geometric constraint provides a quantitative information-geometric characterization of thermal SW-SSB.

papers.title: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding
papers.abstract: Visual perception is evolving from passive recognition toward active, task-oriented observation. We investigate GUI grounding as a scalable source of spatial supervision for learning observation behaviors that transfer beyond interfaces. We introduce LBS (Look Beyond Screens), a vision-language model trained through supervised initialization on teacher-generated GUI grounding trajectories, followed by reinforcement learning for multi-turn crop-and-inspect decisions. Under fixed inference settings, LBS models based on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B consistently improve over their corresponding baselines. Gains beyond supervised fine-tuning transfer to PerceptionBench for both backbones and to HR-Bench and ChartQAPro for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, supporting observation strategies that generalize beyond GUI-specific imitation. Further analysis suggests complementary roles for the two stages: SFT establishes visual inspection primitives, while RL improves their downstream effectiveness. These findings support GUI grounding as a practical supervision paradigm for transferable active visual perception and broader multimodal reasoning. Our code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/inclusionAI/UI-Venus/tree/LBS and https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/LBS-27B, respectively.

papers.title: Certification Time for Weak-Force-Mediated Entanglement between Levitated Particles
papers.abstract: Certifying motional entanglement generated by weak forces between levitated nanoparticles requires distinguishing entangled from separable states using finite, noisy measurement records. We show that the number of measurements required to certify Gaussian entanglement can vary among equally entangled states, and quantify this variation. We derive an attainable lower bound showing that, near the separability threshold, the required number of measurements diverges inversely with the square of the distance from this threshold. We translate the required number of measurements into an experimental certification time, comparing two protocols under comparable experimental conditions: release--recapture, in which particles evolve freely before measurement, and continuous monitoring, in which the steady state is measured continuously. We find that release--recapture enables entanglement certification at interaction strengths several orders of magnitude weaker. Moreover, minimizing certification time can favor states with less entanglement, revealing a trade-off between entanglement generation and its certification. These results highlight the role of certification in the design and optimization of ongoing efforts to probe weak-force-mediated entanglement between levitated nanoparticles.

papers.title: First-Principles Investigation of Irida-Graphane: A Wide-Band-Gap Semiconductor Derived from Irida-Graphene
papers.abstract: Opening a band gap in metallic two-dimensional carbon allotropes is an important step toward their use in electronic and optoelectronic devices, and full hydrogenation has proven to be an effective route to achieve it. Here, we propose irida-graphane, the fully hydrogenated derivative of the irida-graphene, a monolayer composed of three-, six-, and eight-membered rings, and investigate its structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical properties using density functional theory (DFT) at the PBE and HSE06 levels combined with phonon and \textit{ab initio} molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. All carbon atoms adopt $sp^3$ hybridization, with the hydrogen atoms of the three- and six-membered rings bonded to opposite sides of a buckled carbon framework, and the lattice parameter contracts by 4.3% with respect to irida-graphene. The hydrogenation energy of $-0.53$ eV/H indicates that the hydrogenation of irida-graphene from molecular hydrogen is exothermic. The absence of imaginary phonon frequencies confirms the dynamical stability of irida-graphane, and AIMD simulations show that its structure remains intact at temperatures up to 2000 K. Irida-graphane is mechanically isotropic, with an in-plane stiffness of approximately 156 N/m, a Poisson's ratio of approximately 0.1, and critical strains of approximately 20%. Hydrogenation transforms the metallic parent structure into a semiconductor with an indirect band gap of 4.68 eV (PBE) and 6.0 eV (HSE06). Irida-graphane is transparent in the visible range, with reflectivity below 0.3%, and absorbs strongly in the deep ultraviolet, with absorption coefficients of the order of $10^{5} - 10^{6}$ cm$^{-1}$. These results suggest irida-graphane as a candidate wide-gap material for ultraviolet optoelectronics and transparent coatings.

papers.title: On 2-loop AdS$_2$ superstring partition function in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times CP^3$
papers.abstract: We revisit the 2-loop computation of the partition function of the GS superstring expanded near the AdS$_2$ surface in AdS$_5\times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times {\rm CP}^3$, dual to $\frac{1}{2}$ BPS circular Wilson loop in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM and ABJM theories. In arXiv:2601.08809 it was done in AdS$_5\times S^5$ using dimensional regularization and a UV pole was found. Since dimensional regularization is problematic for the GS string, here we use a heat-kernel cutoff instead. Then the contribution of the local path integral measure, proportional to $δ(0)$, can no longer be ignored. We show that it cancels the $δ(0)$ terms coming from the quartic interactions in the action, leaving the square of the difference ${\rm Str}\,E$ between the regularized numbers of bosonic and fermionic modes. The result is thus UV finite, the pole of arXiv:2601.08809 being an artefact of dimensional regularization. If all fields are regularized with the same smearing kernel, ${\rm Str}\,E=0$ and the 2-loop coefficient $f_2$ vanishes, in tension with $f_2=\frac{3}{32π^2}$ in SYM theory. In the AdS$_4\times{\rm CP}^3$ case the same cancellation leaves a finite term proportional to the square of the coincident value of the massless 2d fermion Green's function, giving, ironically, $f_2=\frac{3}{32π^2}$ instead of $f_2=0$ required by localization. This term is the level-zero (string) part of the result of arXiv:2609.14497 for the AdS$_2\times S^1$ M2 brane in AdS$_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, where it is cancelled by the higher $S^1$ modes, which also remove a finite mass shift of the massless fermion in conflict with the AdS$_2$ supersymmetry. This suggests that the type II string path integral measure should contain an extra contribution, supplied in the IIA case by the parent M2 brane; in the AdS$_5\times S^5$ case it is still to be identified and may resolve the remaining 2-loop mismatch with localization.

papers.title: Threshold Compatibility and Support-Selection Diagnostics in Neural Discovery of Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Accurate regression need not yield the correct equation after support selection. For a median/sample-standard-deviation threshold in neural PDE discovery, we derive an exact two-signal retention boundary and a complete-vector perturbation bound. Exact advection-diffusion libraries lose diffusion despite coefficient recovery to numerical precision. True-support refits of forty saved sparse states reduce diffusion error without restoring all derivative accuracy. A fixed sequential threshold ridge comparator recovers exact support in sixty ideal controls but selects extra terms in every learned state. All-fold correct-support candidates are rejected by conditional validation; post hoc energy pooling preserves their higher minimum loss in all sixty states. Supplied-support estimates outperform unchanged selected equations in all 240 physical-residual comparisons on four unused analytic trajectories. With coefficients, observation points and weights fixed, exact replacement of the learned library and target reverses their learned-row ordering in 59/60 states. Weighting both losses also fails the specified Burgers diffusion-benefit criterion at every tested budget. These finite diagnostics distinguish threshold incompatibility, refit damage and score rejection; they establish neither automatic correction nor general recovery or predictive stability.

papers.title: TriDifNet: A Unified Three-Task Diffusion Network for End-to-End RGB-T Perception
papers.abstract: Infrared--visible (IR--VIS) multi-modal perception supports robust scene understanding under challenging illumination. Infrared and visible images are often misaligned due to platform motion, viewpoint changes, and modality-dependent distortions, causing registration errors to propagate into subsequent fusion and detection stages. We propose TriDifNet, a unified three-task diffusion network for end-to-end RGB-T perception. To the best of our knowledge, TriDifNet is the first diffusion-based network that jointly optimizes registration, fusion, and detection for misaligned RGB-T pedestrian perception. TriDifNet consists of three diffusion-based modules, i.e., the Registration Diffusion Module (RegDM), the Fusion Diffusion Module (FusDM), and the Detection Diffusion Module (DetDM). RegDM aligns the unaligned infrared image to the optical reference by estimating a dense deformation field. FusDM performs residual conditional diffusion to generate a detection-oriented fused representation with optical structural cues and complementary infrared saliency. DetDM formulates pedestrian detection as an iterative denoising process in bounding-box space. To couple the three tasks, TriDifNet introduces a closed-loop optimization mechanism, where detection semantics guide fusion and registration, and the fusion result further regularizes geometric alignment. A stage-wise progressive training strategy and a lightweight Nash multi-task learning (Nash-MTL)-based late-stage refinement are further adopted to balance registration, fusion, and detection optimization. Extensive experiments on the KAIST multispectral pedestrian benchmark show that TriDifNet achieves superior downstream detection performance under misaligned RGB-T settings. Against strong system-level competitors, TriDifNet achieves 65.44\% Recall, 57.55\% mAP$_{50}$, and 26.83\% mAP$_{50:95}$.

papers.title: SplatScout: Query-Driven Part-Level Referring Segmentation in Gaussian Scenes
papers.abstract: Existing referring segmentation methods on Gaussian scenes primarily target whole objects, relying on segmenter-generated candidates from which a vision-language model (VLM) selects. Such predetermined fixed candidates may omit fine-grained parts needed as targets or cues for identifying objects. We introduce SplatScout, a query-driven, closed-loop approach that places perception under VLM control. The model actively selects views, directs segmentation, and inspects rendered 3D results to refine its predictions. For part-level evaluation, we introduce PartRef-ScanNet++, comprising 261 manually verified queries across 12 ScanNet++ scenes with mesh-derived ground truth. On PartRef-ScanNet++, SplatScout achieves 0.538 mIoU, substantially outperforming existing methods. Ablations demonstrate the benefits of iterative refinement, while comparisons across VLM backbones highlight the importance of effective tool-feedback utilization. SplatScout also achieves higher scores on four existing referring benchmarks. Code and the PartRef-ScanNet++ benchmark are available at https://github.com/kaust-violab/SplatScout.

papers.title: Large-bulk-viscosity limit for two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluids with vacuum
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid system on the torus $\mathbb T^2$. The initial density is bounded and nonnegative and may contain vacuum, while the initial velocity and microrotation belong to $H^1(\mathbb T^2)$. For sufficiently large bulk viscosity $ν$, we prove the global-in-time existence of solutions without a smallness assumption on the $H^1$ size of the data, provided that the initial compressible component is well prepared in the sense that $\sqrtν\|\operatorname{div}u_0\|_{L^2}$ is uniformly bounded. The proof combines the effective viscous flux with a coupled energy scheme that exploits the vorticity--microrotation dissipation at both the basic and material-derivative levels. For the linear pressure law, we also prove uniqueness in the stated solution class by means of a coupled backward parabolic problem, logarithmic interpolation, and Osgood's lemma. For fixed initial data with $\operatorname{div}u_0=0$, we also justify the limit $ν\to\infty$: every sequence of the corresponding solutions admits a subsequence converging to a solution of the two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible micropolar system.

papers.title: A Two-Stage Optimization Framework for Real-World Large-Scale University Course Timetabling Based on Orthogonalized Hierarchical Modeling and Conflict-Driven ALNS Repair
papers.abstract: University course timetabling is a large-scale combinatorial optimization problem involving strongly coupled temporal and resource constraints. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization framework for real-world large-scale university course timetabling, integrating orthogonalized hierarchical modeling with conflict-driven adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) repair. The first stage performs global course-level optimization, while the second identifies residual conflicts through a conflict graph and localizes them into connected conflict regions. The Course--Occurrence--Session representation provides the structural basis for multi-granularity repair, which employs Cluster-, Course-, Occurrence-, and Session-level destroy operators within the ALNS framework, followed by fine-grained greedy repair. The framework is evaluated on a real-world university timetabling instance involving 3,073 course groups, 8,015 scheduling events, 998 student classes, and 1,511 instructors. Ablation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of hierarchical repair granularity and adaptive operator selection. Across ten independent runs, the ALNS + Greedy framework achieves a mean residual conflict count of 18.50, compared with 172 for deterministic Greedy-only repair under the same initial scheduling conditions, representing an 89.24\% reduction. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed conflict-driven hierarchical repair framework for large-scale university course timetabling.

papers.title: Operator Barron Regularity for Elliptic Equations and Application to Neural Operator Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a spectral Barron regularity framework for nonlinear operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces. Using Hilbert-valued Fourier representations of finite-dimensional input truncations, we establish bounds that are uniform in the input truncation dimension and prove arbitrary-order Barron regularity for a class of elliptic solution operators. Second, we use this operator Barron regularity to derive approximation error bounds for an FNO-type neural operator, with explicit dependence on the input truncation dimension, output reconstruction dimension, and network width. For a fixed input truncation dimension, optimizing the neural approximation bound over the Barron regularity order yields stretched-exponential decay of the approximation error in the network width. We also show some numerical experiments to support the predicted rate.

papers.title: New inhomogeneous Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with large symmetry group
papers.abstract: We study compact non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds endowed with an automorphism group acting with cohomogeneity one. We prove that the Lie algebra of this group is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ or $\mathbb R^2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$, provided that the Bismut connection is not flat. In the first case, we explicitly describe all these structures up to homothety and biholomorphic isometry. We also construct explicit families of complete non-compact examples. The resulting non-Bismut-flat threefolds have non-constant scalar curvature and restricted Bismut holonomy $T^1\subset \mathrm{SU}(3)$, and include examples on $S^3\times S^3$ and complete examples on $S^3\times S^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$. Finally, we construct a smooth deformation of a Bismut-flat Samelson structure on $S^3\times S^3$ through non-Bismut-flat Bismut Hermitian-Einstein structures whose complex structures are not compatible with any Bismut-flat metric.

papers.title: A Comparison of Electric-Field Profile Reconstruction Methods based on the E-FISH Diagnostic
papers.abstract: Electric-field-induced second harmonic generation (EFISH) is a non-intrusive, non-resonant technique for measuring electric fields in moderate-to-atmospheric pressure plasmas. However, its nonlinear, path-integrated nature introduces measurement uncertainty, preventing a unique relationship between the measured signal and local electric field. One approach to overcome this limitation is to acquire spatial EFISH profiles and invert them to reconstruct the underlying electric-field distribution. Although several inversion methods have been employed, their reconstruction accuracy and overall performance have yet to be systematically evaluated. This study compares three methods: machine learning, linear inversion, and Abel inversion, using EFISH measurements from four electrode geometries with distinct electric-field distributions. Their performance is evaluated in terms of reconstruction accuracy, robustness to sparse data and noise, and ability to reconstruct asymmetric profiles. All three methods successfully reconstruct electric-field profiles, but exhibit distinct advantages and limitations. Machine learning provides high accuracy, computational speed, and noise resilience, but performs poorly on profiles that differ substantially from its training data, particularly asymmetric profiles. Linear inversion accommodates a broader range of field distributions but is sensitive to the initial profile. Abel inversion is limited to axisymmetric fields but performs well for horizontal field polarization. The complementary limitations of machine learning and linear inversion motivate a potential hybrid approach for reconstructing electric fields with unknown spatial distributions. Overall, this study identifies key trade-offs among the methods and provides guidance for selecting suitable reconstruction strategies under different measurement conditions.

papers.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification
papers.abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. This work presents two compact spiking neural networks (SNNs) matched to their target hardware: ConvSNN, which maps to the Matrix Vector Processor (MVP) of an EFM32PG28 microcontroller, and StreamSNN, which processes one waveform value per timestep using learned time constants and fixed synaptic delays for a dedicated SKY130 circuit. Evaluated on cells unseen during training, ConvSNN achieves a CS F1 of 0.873 with 1,018 parameters and StreamSNN 0.837 with 527 parameters, both with eight-bit weights. On the microcontroller, MVP acceleration reduces ConvSNN latency by 62.3\% and extends estimated battery life to 33.73~hours on a 50~mAh battery. In SKY130, StreamSNN occupies 0.173~mm$^2$ and consumes 0.46~$μ$J per event, with 0.2~ms of computation within an 8.3~ms end-to-end latency.

papers.title: Text Generation in Low-Resource Languages Using Human-Curated Vocabularies
papers.abstract: Synthetic text generation offers a promising approach to alleviating data scarcity in low-resource languages. However, its effectiveness is inherently limited for languages that are scarcely represented, or entirely absent, in an LLM's pretraining data. At the same time, many such languages have human-curated vocabularies that provide rich lexical and semantic information, often accompanied by grammatical information such as part-of-speech labels. In this work, we ask whether LLMs can leverage these resources to generate coherent text in extremely low-resource and unseen languages. We introduce a framework that combines human-curated vocabularies with a small number of human-written exemplars that provide syntactic signals, while sampling candidate words according to a Zipfian distribution. Across languages with varying levels of resource availability, we evaluate the generated text using lexical diversity, off-target ratio, and human judgments of fluency. Our results show that reasoning-enabled LLMs can generate fluent text even in extremely low-resource languages, with particularly strong results at the sentence level and promising performance at the paragraph level. Our findings highlight a practical pathway for bootstrapping synthetic data in low-resource languages, expanding the amount of usable text even when existing digital resources are extremely limited. Our source code is available at https://github.com/michaelsinanta/vocab2text.

papers.title: Probing new $C\!P$-violating sources in $Λ_b\toΛ_c\ell^-\barν_\ell$
papers.abstract: While baryonic $C\!P$ violation has been observed, its potential to reveal new physics beyond the sensitivity of mesonic decays remains an open question. We investigate this potential within semileptonic $b\to c\ell\barν_\ell$ transitions by comparing the angular distributions of $Λ_b\toΛ_c(\toΛπ)\ell^-\barν_\ell$ and $\bar B\to D^*(\to Dπ)\ell^-\barν_\ell$ utilizing lattice-QCD form factors. We perform a global fit to $R(D^{(*)})$ alongside auxiliary $C\!P$-even measurements to delineate the phenomenologically viable parameter space for new-physics Wilson coefficients. Leveraging these allowed ranges and the lattice inputs, we evaluate the complementary sensitivity of both angular distributions to novel weak phases. We demonstrate that the baryonic decay mode probes combinations of Wilson coefficients that remain inaccessible in mesonic angular distributions, thereby providing critical supplementary information for identifying new physics.

papers.title: A Counterexample to KL1 Completeness and a Complete Disjunctive Calculus
papers.abstract: The logic KL$_1$ of Evans, Sergot and Stephenson formalizes Kant's rules as conditional imperatives $B \square\to C$ and permissives $B \diamond\to C$ over acts. Its consequence relation is operational: a rule follows from a set of rules when adjoining it leaves the set of outcomes unchanged for every input. The authors proved their calculus sound and conjectured that it is complete. We show that the conjecture fails: for distinct atoms $b,c,d$ the rules $\top \diamond\to b \lor d$, $b \diamond\to c$, $d \diamond\to c$ and $c \square\to b \lor d$ entail $\top \diamond\to c$, which is not derivable. Non-derivability is proved by an invariant that holds at every derivation depth and for arbitrary intermediate atoms. The obstruction is the side condition of may-trans, which requires each new act to bring with it a single intermediary act. Replacing it by a disjunctive side condition yields may-trans-disj, a strict generalization from which the original rule is derivable. Using a local characterization of entailment, we prove the repaired calculus sound for arbitrary sets of rules and complete for finite ones, and we show that, with finite inputs, completeness cannot be extended to infinite sets. The main results on KL$_1$ are formalized in Agda. For KL$_2$ we observe that the published reduction to KL$_1$ passes through infinite rule sets; re-establishing the decomposition for finite rule sets, we prove that KL$_2$ with the disjunctive rule is sound and complete for finite sets of rules. We close with remarks on KL$_3$ and on the significance of completeness for the relation between the operational and the inferential questions of Kant's logic.

papers.title: Finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebras and fixed-point combinators
papers.abstract: We study algebras for the $\mathbf{BM}$-, $\mathbf{BI}$-, and $\mathbf{BMI}$-fragments of combinatory logic, where $\mathbf{B} xyz \to_{w} x\left(yz\right)$, $\mathbf{M} x \to_{w} xx$ and $\mathbf{I} x \to_{w} x$. We prove that every finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ contains an element $Y$ satisfying $Yx = x\left(Yx\right)$ for all $x\in A$. Moreover, a single closed $\mathbf{BM}$-term represents such an element in every finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebra. On the other hand, we show that there exists an infinite $\mathbf{BMI}$-algebra with no such element. Consequently, the variety of $\mathbf{BM}$-algebras is not generated by finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebras. We also characterise finite $\mathbf{BI}$-algebras as finite semigroups with two distinguished left units $B$ and $I$, and finite $\mathbf{BMI}$-algebras as finite idempotent semigroups with three distinguished left units $B$, $M$ and $I$.

papers.title: Predicate Neuron: Differentiable Quantization of Predicate Relations in Gradient-based Learning
papers.abstract: In machine learning, symbolic reasoning approaches often rely on static architectures that hinder integration into deep neural networks and gradient-based optimization. To address this, we introduce the Native Predicate Neuron, a differentiable logic-reasoning neural module that enriches standard architectures with symbolic reasoning capabilities via first-order logic quantization. The proposed neuron models relational logic by learning to alternate between operations using a single trainable parameter. It features a tailored gradient mechanism with a dual-nature formulation: executing hard logical operations during training while maintaining differentiability for backpropagation. By quantizing both its input and choice state, the Predicate Neuron approximates continuous and non-continuous functions, effectively resolving discontinuities that standard deep learning architectures struggle with. We evaluate the Predicate Neuron across Fully-Connected, Convolutional, Recurrent, and Transformer architectures on benchmarks like MNIST and Wikitext. Results show that incorporating Predicate Neurons accelerates convergence, boosts accuracy, and lowers loss in general, with particularly strong improvements in tasks requiring monotonic reasoning or handling discontinuities. Overall, the Predicate Neuron natively integrates into standard neural networks to enable fuzzy logic operations and is available in Keras and PyTorch.

papers.title: Reggeized $K^*(892)$ exchange in $π^- p \to K^0 Λ$ and implications for fixed-target measurements
papers.abstract: The two-body $π^- p \to K^0 Λ$ reaction provides a clean channel for studying strangeness production and producing tagged hyperon $Λ$ samples. We describe its total cross section over the $π^-$ beam momentum $2.6 \leq p_{π, {\rm lab}} \leq 6.0~{\rm GeV}/c$ using a single Reggeized $t$-channel $K^*(892)$ exchange without polarization. We also examine the implications for future fixed-target measurements. An idealized event sample is used to determine the laboratory momentum and polar-angle distributions of the charged particles from $K_S^0 \to π^+ π^-$ and $Λ\to p π^-$. The $K_S^0$ decayed two pions are strongly forward, whereas the proton and pion from the $Λ$ decay extend to larger angles and lower momenta. These distributions provide a kinematic baseline for future acceptance and tracking studies.

papers.title: A First-Step Bias Restores Lost Diversity in Diffusion Model Distillation
papers.abstract: Distribution-matching distillation enables high-quality image generation in only a few denoising steps. However, distilled student models often map different initial noise samples to similar outputs under the same prompt. To locate where diversity is lost, we compare the teacher and student along the sampling trajectory. The largest measured reduction in the response to different initial noises occurs during the first, high-noise step. When we replace the first step with the teacher's corresponding trajectory and leave the final three student steps unchanged, most of the output diversity returns. This suggests that the first step is a key point for restoring diversity. Motivated by this finding, we introduce \emph{ReSeed}, a post-distillation method that adds a seed-response bias adapter only to the first student step and aligns its velocity with the teacher's first-interval secant velocity. All student weights and later denoising steps remain unchanged. We evaluate ReSeed on three text-to-image models (SD3-Medium, SD3.5-Medium, and FLUX.1-dev) and one text-to-video model (Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B). For a distilled 4-step FLUX.1-dev model, \emph{ReSeed} requires only $0.00196\%$ additional trainable parameters relative to the base model and is trained on 8,000 prompt--noise pairs, while keeping the distilled student fully frozen and requiring no target images, perceptual losses, or adversarial losses. It improves DINO diversity by $48.3\%$ while maintaining competitive visual quality. These results show that substantial diversity can be recovered through a lightweight, data-efficient tuning of only the first denoising step, without finetuning the full student model.

papers.title: RAVEN: A Unified Active SLAM System for Rapid Autonomous Visual Exploration with Aerial Robots under Localization Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Active simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) addresses the problem of planning robot motion to build complete and accurate maps of unknown environments through efficient exploration while maintaining high localization accuracy. This raises a dilemma between exploring unknown spaces to expand coverage and exploiting visited regions to perform active loop closures. Despite numerous prior works on ground robots, aerial robots with high agility and constrained sensor suites face more significant localization drift and thereby demand dedicated active SLAM planning. Moreover, a unified strategy that adapts performance based on task-specific priorities remains an open question. In this article, we introduce RAVEN, a unified active SLAM framework for Rapid Autonomous Visual ExploratioN using quadrotors, which systematically accounts for localization uncertainty. The framework starts with identifying frontiers and active loop closure candidates, from which global tour candidates are generated. These candidates are evaluated using a utility vector that separately quantifies exploration efficiency and localization accuracy, and the final tour is selected according to a prioritization parameter ranging from $[0,1]$. Finally, a perception-aware navigation planner generates smooth execution trajectories that minimize visual state estimation error based on the online Fisher information field that provides visual localization information in real-time. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate that RAVEN outperforms state-of-the-art active SLAM methods, highlighting its advantages in producing a spectrum of performance across prioritizations. Fully onboard field experiments with a customized stereo-inertial quadrotor further validate its practical applicability in challenging environments. The source code will be released to benefit the community.

papers.title: Decoupling Procedural and Outcome Fairness in Seed Allocation for Influence Maximization
papers.abstract: On online social platforms, equal seed access to interventions can yield unequal group outcomes through social spillovers, so an access audit alone can miss outcome disparities. We characterise this trade-off through an exact allocation-structure decomposition and a sharp first-moment floor for graph-independent seeding under additive spillovers on stochastic block networks. Decoupled Procedural Allocation (DPA) combines group quotas with selection by seeds' contributions to each group's outcome. Rankings balance total outcome against disparity, and within-quota exchanges reduce the gap. Computable bounds quantify retained total outcome. DPA achieves the smallest mean outcome gap among the compared methods at the common access tolerances on both development and prospective suites. Exposure and independent-cascade studies show how the propagation mechanism changes this trade-off. On Pokec, DPA nearly equalises modelled gender outcomes at the closest access-parity quota while preserving most of the degree-based allocation's total outcome.

papers.title: Beyond Similarity Search: Knowledge Graph Metadata Enrichment for Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: A key challenge of RAG systems is retrieving information from enterprise documents created by multiple teams over time, where it is not possible to enrich the information using the latest information and metadata available outside the scope of organizational documentation responsibility. We investigated whether using a knowledge graph to store metadata and frequently changing information would improve upon knowledge retrieval over similarity search over embeddings. To perform the experiment, we created a snapshot of the SEC EDGAR dataset for a quarter, comprising 167,050 filings from 10,511 companies and 508,714 embedded chunks of risk-factor text. To simulate the enrichment, we created a knowledge graph of 430,257 nodes and 561,144 edges carrying an accession number on every edge. To evaluate the gain obtained via a graph-based design, we evaluated three architectures: text-to-SQL over typed columns, dense-vector RAG with HNSW cosine search, and a two-stage GraphRAG design. All architectures share the same model and temperature to allow comparison. Results are scored programmatically by an LLM as judge over 20 questions divided across four categories, each question asked three times. GraphRAG solved 16 of 20 questions on all three attempts, compared to 10 for text-to-SQL and 3 for vector RAG. GraphRAG lost on structured aggregation queries. Vector RAG lost the single-document category it was expected to win, passing 3 of 15 where GraphRAG passed 15 of 15, because company attribution is not recoverable from cosine similarity at this scale. All six confident falsehoods in the benchmark were text-to-SQL conflating distinct people who share a surname, the failure that resolving identity to an identifier before reading any text prevents structurally; GraphRAG made none. We claim no advantage beyond this corpus, this model and this question set.

papers.title: Spectral delocalization and central limit theorems for Fourier functionals of stationary Gaussian fields
papers.abstract: We characterize Gaussian fluctuations of Fourier-Hermite functionals of stationary Gaussian fields on locally compact Abelian groups via spectral delocalization: conditional on the total spectral sum being near the probed frequency, no partial sum concentrates. Under suitable assumptions, this reduces Gaussian convergence to small-ball estimates for convolution powers of the spectral measure, without model-specific contraction estimates. On $\mathbb T^d$, the criterion yields CLTs at every fixed frequency for band-limited fields and random trigonometric polynomials, and extends the known failure of Gaussian convergence for planar arithmetic random waves from the fourth chaos to all even orders $q\ge4$. On $\mathbb R^d$ and $\mathbb Z^d$, we establish a Breuer-Major theorem for Fourier functionals at every frequency with nonzero limiting variance. Cyclical long-memory models exhibit frequency-dependent Gaussian convergence. We also establish CLTs and variance asymptotics for singular continuous spectral measures, including those of stationary Gaussian solutions of linear PDEs. At zero frequency, weak Ahlfors regularity of the spectral support and an $L^2$ density suffice for second-chaos CLTs, covering fractal sets, the Airy surface of Gaussian sea waves, and smooth compact manifolds. For a class of smooth hypersurfaces, we obtain the same variance rates and CLTs known for classical nonlinear functionals of Berry's random wave model. Finally, for random waves with spherical spectral densities bounded above and below, we classify Gaussian convergence at every frequency $\|z\|\le q$: it fails only for the planar second chaos when $0<\|z\|<2$.

papers.title: X-ray Emission Study of TeV Blazars
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a systematic X-ray study of 85 TeV-detected blazars based on archival \emph{Swift}-XRT and \emph{NuSTAR} observations available up to May 2024. We derive unabsorbed X-ray fluxes and photon indices through spectral fitting, and investigate their light curves, spectral energy distributions, flux distributions, power spectral densities, and flux-index correlations. Using the fractional variability method, we identify 78 sources as variable in the soft X-ray band and 14 sources as variable in the hard X-ray band. For well-sampled soft X-ray light curves, the flux distributions are generally better described by log-normal functions, while the PSD slopes span $β_{\rm PSD}=0.1$--$1.6$, with most values between 1.0 and 1.6, where the PSD is defined as $P(f)\propto f^{-β_{\rm PSD}}$. We find positive correlations between TeV and X-ray luminosities, supporting a leptonic emission scenario. We also find a correlation between X-ray and disk luminosities, whereas no significant correlation is found between X-ray luminosity and black hole mass.

papers.title: Self-Regularized Flow Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce SERF (Self-Regularized Flow Language Models), a simple self-supervised framework for improving continuous diffusion language models by exploiting the denoising trajectory itself. While continuous flow-based language models offer a promising alternative to autoregressive generation, their training objectives typically rely on supervision from clean target tokens, leaving the denoising trajectory underexploited as a learning signal. SERF addresses this limitation through noisy-to-clean self-distillation: an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher receives a cleaner version of the student's noisy input along the same interpolation path and provides additional supervision. We investigate two variants: SERF-L, which aligns the student's intermediate representations with deeper teacher representations, and SERF-P, which aligns their output token distributions, either at the student's output or at an early student layer. All variants augment the standard training objective without requiring external pretrained models or modifying the inference procedure. Experiments across three continuous language-model paradigms (one-hot FLM, latent ELF, and hyper-spherical S-FLM) demonstrate substantial improvements in training efficiency, generation quality, and few-step generation. In particular, SERF achieves up to 7.7x wall-clock training acceleration on OpenWebText, improves MAUVE by 24.3% and GSM8K accuracy by up to 28.8%, and matches baseline performance with up to 64x fewer sampling steps. These results establish noisy-to-clean self-distillation as an effective approach to improving continuous diffusion language models.

papers.title: Generative quantum extreme learning machines
papers.abstract: Training the circuit of a quantum generative model is hampered by barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with the number of qubits. In the present work we propose a generative protocol based on the paradigm of quantum extreme learning machines, in which the circuit is never trained. A random latent vector is encoded into a quantum state, evolved with a fixed unitary and measured, and only a linear output layer is trained. The encoding of the latent variable determines the functions available to the model, while the unitary decides which combinations of them are seen by the trained layer. With the help of Pauli propagation we show that for a Clifford unitary each feature is a single product of sines and cosines of the encoded angles, so that a Clifford circuit, even a strongly entangling one, does not create new functions. Doping the circuit with $T$ gates mixes these products and changes the nonstabilizerness of the state, but the space of functions remains the one fixed by the encoding. For brickworks of Haar-random two-qubit gates the features are no longer single products, and their variation with the latent variable decreases with the depth of the circuit. For the proposed encoding and for one- and two-dimensional distributions, generated both from expectation values and from single measurements, neither the entanglement produced by a Clifford reservoir nor the additional nonstabilizerness of Haar-random brickworks systematically improves the generator, and a reservoir with no gates at all is competitive with entangling circuits.

papers.title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Features in a $Λ>0$ Universe
papers.abstract: A complete understanding of cosmology, from its earliest epoch all the way to the current dark energy dominated era, requires the development of a mathematical framework that incorporates quantum features in an expanding universe. Such a framework, alongside a description of the underlying degrees of freedom, is so far lacking. Several of the pertinent challenges and puzzles already arise upon considering even the most idealised model of an expanding universe --- the de Sitter spacetime and fluctuations thereof. In these lectures, we review some elementary ideas of the de Sitter physics, passing through the representation theory of the de Sitter group, aspects of canonical quantum gravity, all the way to attempts in describing quasi-local features. Throughout, we highlight open problems that motivate ongoing efforts to understand quantum gravity and cosmology in universes with $Λ>0$. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School: The Disordered Universe 2025 from 21 July to 1 August 2025.

papers.title: Multibranch Ensemble Head in Vision Foundation Models for Efficient Cucumber Phenological Stage Classification
papers.abstract: Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) pretrained with self-supervised learning, such as DINOv2, provide highly transferable features, yet adapting them to small, domain-shifted datasets is still challenging. We propose a regularizing multibranch ensemble head: a training and inference scheme that pairs low- and high-capacity branches, samples a single branch stochastically at each training step, and averages both branches in probability space at inference. The design adds negligible parameters and essentially no inference overhead over a single heavy head, while improving the accuracy-efficiency trade-off under data-scarce conditions. Accurate classification of plant growth stages is critical for precision agriculture, enabling timely decisions on fertilization, irrigation, and harvesting. Therefore, as a challenging practical case we use cucumber phenological stage classification, in which flowers and fruits are frequently occluded by foliage, and stage transitions manifest primarily as subtle changes in leaf morphology. The NALEF Food Safety dataset contains images of five cucumber growth stages captured under diverse real-world conditions. On it we evaluate a broad range of backbones, including DINOv2 and DINOv3 ViT and ConvNeXt variants, against strongly supervised counterparts (ResNet, EfficientNet, ViT). The proposed DINOv2 ViT-S with multibranch head achieves a Macro F1 of 0.978 and Cohen's Kappa of 0.971, matching the performance of models more than ten times larger in parameters and GFlops, while requiring only 12.2 GFlops and 22.3M parameters, making it deployable on smartphones and edge devices for phenological stage classification.

papers.title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
papers.abstract: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemerédi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.

papers.title: Easier parameter scans with hmcdj
papers.abstract: We present hmcdj, a new tool developed to ease the process of generating large numbers of gauge ensembles for a given theory. Building on top of the Grid library, hmcdj allows quick specification of lattice gauge theories in C++ with minimal boilerplate, and precise specification of per-ensemble parameters to be controlled at run time from a YAML input file. Additionally, it supports many quality-of-life features for managing large numbers of running jobs, including automatic tuning of the molecular dynamics step size to control the Metropolis acceptance rate; output of ILDG-compliant data; and integration with HPC schedulers to dynamically adapt the target trajectory count of a job to match its time limits. hmcdj is openly available under the GPLv2 license, and welcomes new contributions.

papers.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning
papers.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. In such domains, frontier models tend to give generic answers. Knowledge graphs (KGs) can ground LLM reasoning. Because a graph is too large to provide in full, typical LLM+KG systems preselect a portion, deciding relevance before reasoning begins. Here we train a compact model, Prospector, to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step, seeking evidence in light of what it has already found. Prospector calls a small set of tools one at a time to progressively build its context, and answers with a chain of evidence that can be checked edge by edge against what its tools retrieved from the graph. On a knowledge graph built from the semiconductor-manufacturing literature, Prospector approaches the strongest off-the-shelf models given the same graph and tools, and it far exceeds off-the-shelf models answering closed-book or from a pre-selected portion of the graph. Although trained only on the semiconductor graph, Prospector transfers to unseen knowledge graphs from three other distinct fields: bio-inspired materials, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and materials properties. Served on a single GPU, Prospector answers faster and at a fraction of the cost of a hosted service, while keeping proprietary data on the owner's hardware. We find that the policy's latent state is indicative of its next move on both seen and unseen graphs, and modulating the latent state can steer the policy from one behavior mode to another. These results suggest a practical LLM + KG paradigm for scientific and engineering reasoning over private data, in which a compact model trained on a graph from published literature transfers its traversal to unseen graphs that stay with their owners.

papers.title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
papers.abstract: We establish an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. The classical sampler--extractor equivalence is established by a seminal work of Zuckerman (Random Structures & Algorithms, 1997). Using this equivalence, we construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity via constructing quantum-proof extractors. Specifically for matrix dimension $D$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ and failure probability $δ\leq\varepsilon$, our matrix sampler uses $m+O_α(\log(D/δ))$ random bits and $O_α(\varepsilon^{-2-α}\log^{1+α}(D/δ))$ samples, for any constant $α>0$. Compared with the matrix sampler of Xun and Zuckerman (CCC 2025), our construction has improvements in two aspects. Under the same optimal random seed length, we can replace the $\operatorname{poly} D$ dependence in the number of samples by $O(\log^{1-γ} D)$. Under the same scale of sample size, we can remove their $\log\log D$ factor in the length of the random seed. Our underlying strong quantum-proof extractor has output length $n-O_α(a+\log(1/η))$ and seed length at most $(1+α)\log a+(2+α)\log(1/η)+O_α(1)$ for $n$-bit sources with conditional min-entropy $n-a$ and error $η$. We also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors for every constant entropy rate, for any error as small as $2^{-Ω(n)}$, having optimal seed length $O(\log(n/η))$ and output length $Ω(n)$, improving previous constructions.

papers.title: SFE-O: An Ontology for Knowledge-Grounded AI in Supercritical CO$_2$ Biomass Extraction and Fractionation
papers.abstract: Supercritical CO$_2$ extraction (CO$_2$-SFE) offers a sustainable route for recovering high-value compounds from biomass while limiting the use of conventional organic solvents, but its design and interpretation require heterogeneous knowledge spanning biomass properties, operating conditions, mass transfer, and product fractionation, typically fragmented across technical reports, engineering models, external databases, and expert practice. This paper introduces SFE-O, a modular Web Ontology Language (OWL 2) ontology for supercritical CO$_2$ biomass extraction, structured around interconnected Biomass, Process, and Product dimensions and extended with explicit representations of process topology, parameter provenance, external and internal mass-transfer phenomena, and the Constant Extraction Rate (CER) / Falling Extraction Rate (FER) mechanisms. Computational dependencies among process quantities are represented explicitly, without embedding numerical solving in the ontology, so that input, measured, computed, externally retrieved, and fitted parameters remain traceable. SFE-O reuses established semantic resources (ChEBI, QUDT, OWL-Time, PROV-O) and is evaluated through a worked example that instantiates a real pilot-scale extraction batch, a reasoner-based consistency check, and a competency-question SPARQL query. The resulting knowledge model provides a machine-actionable foundation for querying, consistency checking, and mechanistic explanation of SFE processes, and establishes a knowledge layer that could support future ontology-grounded AI reasoning, a direction this paper motivates but does not evaluate.

papers.title: Finite Element Modeling of Fracture in Brittle Foods with Physically Consistent Parameter Calibration: A Practical Case Study on Cooled Dark Chocolate
papers.abstract: Fracture in food can be undesired during production and transportation but also intended during cutting, grinding or mastication. The associated peak load, the deformation at failure and the resulting fragment geometry are all product properties. This work condenses the modeling of such fracture into a physically rigorous recipe that considers the practical constraints imposed by finite element simulations where necessary and applies idealized theoretical assessments where applicable. Cooled dark chocolate serves as a reproducible model material. Two well-established modeling frameworks for Griffith-type brittle fracture are assessed at an affordable spatial discretization: a sharp-interface and a diffuse phase-field approach. The assessment covers the choice of numerical framework, its discretization and a staged identification of the model parameters. Each parameter is identified from the loading stage that governs it: elastic parameters from pre-crack tension and compression, critical energy release rate from three-point-bending peak force, and the phase-field width last. The phase-field width interferes with the structural response, crack curvature and stress fields, depending on its lower bound set by the affordable spatial resolution. Elastic slope, peak force and crack path therefore cannot be met practically by a single parameter set. The objective must be fixed for the calibration of the model parameters and reported together with the numerical parameters and the boundary value problem.

papers.title: Inverse modelling of a laser-plasma accelerator
papers.abstract: The electron beams of a laser-plasma accelerator depend non-linearly on the laser and gas settings. This dependence is explored using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, and machine-learning models trained on these simulations predict the beam from the settings. Here we address the reverse problem: given a measured beam, which settings produced it? We infer three of them: the gas pressure $p\_1$, the normalised vector potential $a\_0$ and the nitrogen concentration $c\_{N\_2}$. The solution is not guaranteed to be unique. We train an ensemble of mixture density networks that, for each beam, output several possible sets of settings with their probabilities and uncertainties, and test them on simulated beams with realistic measurement noise. On average, the predictions are accurate ($R^2 = 0.91$), yet for about two-thirds of the beams the inferred distribution has two competing solutions. These share nearly the same value of $a\_0^2 p\_1$, which controls how strongly the laser focuses itself in the plasma and, in earlier PALLAS studies, when electrons start to be injected. Keeping this quantity fixed gives beams that are practically indistinguishable with realistic diagnostics. A forward model used as a check removes unphysical solutions but cannot choose between the two plausible ones. We then test two ways to resolve the ambiguity. Adding the full electron energy spectrum improves the mean prediction ($R^2 = 0.94$), mostly through $a\_0$. It changes the weights of the two solutions but does not move them. A second measurement at a deliberately different plasma density is more effective. In paired PIC simulations, it reduces the error on $a\_0$ by a factor of 2.6, whereas repeating the measurement at the same density brings almost no gain.

papers.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known. In this paper, we prove this conjecture completely.

papers.title: Mechanistic Failure Modes of Weight Pruning in Transformer Language Models
papers.abstract: Pruned language models are judged almost entirely by accuracy and perplexity, which assumes that preserved output behaviour implies preserved internal computation. We test this assumption with a factorial pruning study on GPT-2, crossing two importance criteria (magnitude, random), two component types (attention heads, MLP neurons) and three sparsity levels (3%, 50%, 70%). Using the fully characterised indirect object identification (IOI) circuit as ground truth, we measure circuit integrity with activation patching, path patching and direct logit attribution. We find two qualitatively distinct failure modes. Magnitude head pruning >= zeroes the circuit: output-facing heads are removed, and the model falls to near-chance. Magnitude neuron pruning at 30% inverts it: all 26 circuit heads remain intact, but Name Mover contributions flip sign, and the model systematically prefers the wrong name (17.7% accuracy). Perplexity ranks it as less damaged than random head pruning (74.6 vs 140.1). A replication of the Greater-Than circuit shows that the critical component type depends on the circuit's architecture. These results show that output metrics and structural checks can both miss mechanistic damage, motivating circuit-level causal analysis as a complementary evaluation of compressed language models.

papers.title: MCP-Net: Real-Time Coronary Perception Network and Topological Analysis for Robotic Guidewire Navigation
papers.abstract: Coronary guidewire navigation during percutaneous coronary intervention requires continuous interpretation of vessel anatomy, guidewire position, and target stenosis under two-dimensional X-ray fluoroscopy. While existing approaches commonly address vessel segmentation or device localization as separate tasks, a robotic system requires a more structured perception of the coronary scene to support downstream navigation. In this work, we present a simulation-driven framework centered on a Multi-Task Coronary Perception Network (MCP-Net) for robotic guidewire navigation, integrating coronary vessel segmentation, vascular topology extraction, and roadmap generation. Starting from three-dimensional coronary CT angiography, we generate simulated fluoroscopy images containing vascular structures, simulated guidewires, stenotic lesions with varying severity, and diverse vascular geometries, together with simulation-derived ground truth. MCP-Net jointly performs coronary vessel segmentation, guidewire-tip localization, and stenosis localization from a single fluoroscopic frame. These predictions are subsequently converted into a structured vascular graph containing centerlines, bifurcations, endpoints, branch directions, and branch angles. By associating the predicted stenosis with this graph, the framework generates a roadmap from the automatically selected graph root toward the target lesion. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can jointly recover coronary perception targets and transform them into an interpretable vascular representation suitable for downstream robotic navigation.

papers.title: ROAR: Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate Heuristic for Large and Extreme Scale Traveling Repairman Problem
papers.abstract: The Traveling Repairman Problem minimizes cumulative arrival times rather than the total route length, as in the classical Traveling Salesman Problem.
